<p style="margin: 18pt 0pt 0pt;"><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt; font-weight: bold;">Ben Franklin Financial, Inc. </font></p>
<p style="margin: 6pt 0pt 0pt; text-indent: 8%;"><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">Ben Franklin Financial, Inc., a Maryland corporation (&#8220;Ben Franklin Financial&#8221; or the &#8220;Company&#8221;) was organized in September 2014. Upon completion of the mutual-to-stock conversion of Ben Franklin Financial, MHC in January 2015, Ben Franklin Financial became the holding company of Ben Franklin Bank of Illinois (&#8220;Ben Franklin Bank&#8221;) and succeeded to all of the business and operations of Ben Franklin Financial, Inc., a Federal Corporation (&#8220;Ben Franklin-Federal&#8221;) and each of Ben Franklin-Federal and Ben Franklin Financial, MHC ceased to exist. Since the completion of the mutual-to-stock conversion, the Company has not engaged in any significant business activity other than owning the common stock of and having deposits in the Bank. Our executive offices are located at <font class="FactMarked mceNonEditable">830</font> East Kensington Road, Arlington Heights, Illinois <font class="FactMarked mceNonEditable">60004</font>, and our telephone number at that address is (<font class="FactMarked mceNonEditable">847</font>)</font><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">&nbsp;</font><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;"><font class="FactMarked mceNonEditable">398</font>-<font class="FactMarked mceNonEditable">0990</font>. Our Internet address is www.benfrankbank.com. Information on this website is not and should not be considered to be a part of this document. </font></p>
<p style="margin: 18pt 0pt 0pt;"><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt; font-weight: bold;">Ben Franklin Bank of Illinois </font></p>
<p style="margin: 6pt 0pt 0pt; text-indent: 8%;"><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">Ben Franklin Bank of Illinois is a federally-chartered savings bank headquartered in Arlington Heights, Illinois. Ben Franklin Bank was originally founded in <font class="FactMarked mceNonEditable">1893</font> as a building and loan association. </font></p>
<p style="margin: 12pt 0pt 0pt; text-indent: 8%;"><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">Our principal business consists of attracting retail deposits from the general public in our market and investing those deposits, together with funds generated from operations, in <font class="FactMarked mceNonEditable">one</font>- to <font class="FactMarked mceNonEditable">four</font>-family residential mortgage </font></p>
<p style="margin: 0pt;"><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 8pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin: 0pt;"><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 8pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin: 0pt;"><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">loans, commercial real estate loans, multi-family real estate loans, home equity lines of credit and, to a much lesser extent, commercial business loans, construction loans, and consumer loans. In the past we have also made land loans, and we may determine to resume making such loans in the future. We also invest in U.S. government sponsored entity mortgage-backed securities and other securities issued by U.S. government sponsored entities. Our revenues are derived principally from the interest on loans and securities, fees for loan origination services, loan fees, and fees levied on deposit accounts. Our primary sources of funds are deposits and principal and interest payments on loans and securities and to a lesser extent advances from the Federal Home Loan Bank. </font></p>
<p style="margin: 12pt 0pt 0pt; text-indent: 8%;"><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">We conduct our business from our main office and <font class="FactMarked mceNonEditable">one</font> branch office. Both of our offices are located in the northwestern corridor of the Chicago metropolitan area. Ben Franklin Bank&#8217;s executive offices are located at <font class="FactMarked mceNonEditable">830</font> East Kensington Road, Arlington Heights, Illinois <font class="FactMarked mceNonEditable">60004</font>, and our telephone number at that address is (<font class="FactMarked mceNonEditable">847</font>)</font><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">&nbsp;</font><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;"><font class="FactMarked mceNonEditable">398</font>-<font class="FactMarked mceNonEditable">0990</font>. Our Internet address is www.benfrankbank.com. Information on this website is not and should not be considered to be a part of this annual report. </font></p>
<p style="margin: 18pt 0pt 0pt;"><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt; font-weight: bold;">Market Area </font></p>
<p style="margin: 6pt 0pt 0pt; text-indent: 8%;"><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">We conduct business through our main office located at <font class="FactMarked mceNonEditable">830</font> East Kensington Road, Arlington Heights, Illinois and our branch office located at <font class="FactMarked mceNonEditable">3266</font> Kirchoff Road, Rolling Meadows, Illinois. </font></p>
<p style="margin: 12pt 0pt 0pt; text-indent: 8%;"><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">Our offices are located in relatively affluent suburban communities located approximately <font class="FactMarked mceNonEditable">15</font> miles to the northwest of Chicago, Illinois, which is located in Cook County, Illinois. In <font class="FactMarked mceNonEditable">2016</font>, Cook County experienced a <font class="FactMarked mceNonEditable">4.2</font>% increase in median household income and a <font class="FactMarked mceNonEditable">4.9</font>% increase in per capita income compared to <font class="FactMarked mceNonEditable">2015</font>. We believe that Arlington Heights and, to a lesser extent, Rolling Meadows may be classified as &#8220;mature&#8221; suburbs and that more rapid growth is occurring in the counties immediately surrounding Chicago. </font></p>
<p style="margin: 12pt 0pt 0pt; text-indent: 8%;"><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">Our market area has continued to experience a recovery from the economic downturn in 2008 that caused the real estate values to decline for several years after the initial downturn. &nbsp;Sales activity for single family and condominiums during <font class="FactMarked mceNonEditable">2016</font> in the nine county Chicago Primary Statistical Metropolitan Area increased <font class="FactMarked mceNonEditable">4.3</font>% compared to <font class="FactMarked mceNonEditable">2015</font> and the 2016 year-end median price was $<font class="FactMarked mceNonEditable">222,500</font>&nbsp;compared to $<font class="FactMarked mceNonEditable">210,000</font>&nbsp;in 2015 as reported by the Illinois Association of Realtors. This price is still below the market high of $<font class="FactMarked mceNonEditable">247,800</font> in December 2007. </font></p>
<p style="margin: 18pt 0pt 0pt;"><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt; font-weight: bold;">Competition </font></p>
<p style="margin: 6pt 0pt 0pt; text-indent: 8%;"><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">We face intense competition within our market area both in making loans and attracting deposits. The Chicago metropolitan area has a high concentration of financial institutions, including large money center and regional banks, community banks and credit unions, all of which are our competitors to varying degrees. Most of our competitors are significantly larger institutions with greater financial resources than we have, and many offer products and services that we do not or cannot provide. </font></p>
<p style="margin: 12pt 0pt 0pt; text-indent: 8%;"><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">Our competition for loans and deposits comes principally from commercial banks, savings institutions, mortgage banking firms and credit unions. We face additional competition for deposits from short-term money market funds, brokerage firms, mutual funds and insurance companies. Our deposit sources are primarily concentrated in the communities surrounding our banking offices located in Arlington Heights and Rolling Meadows in Cook County, Illinois. As of June</font><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">&nbsp;</font><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;"><font class="FactMarked mceNonEditable">30</font>, <font class="FactMarked mceNonEditable">2016</font>, the latest date for which FDIC data is available, we had approximately <font class="FactMarked mceNonEditable">1.58</font>% of market share in Arlington Heights. As of that same date we had approximately <font class="FactMarked mceNonEditable">1.56</font>% of market share in Rolling Meadows. Our market share in Cook County overall was <font class="FactMarked mceNonEditable">0.03</font>%. </font></p>
<p style="margin: 18pt 0pt 0pt;"><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt; font-weight: bold;">Lending Activities </font></p>
<p style="margin: 6pt 0pt 0pt; text-indent: 8%;"><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt; font-style: italic; font-weight: bold;">General</font><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">. Our principal lending activity is originating and acquiring <font class="FactMarked mceNonEditable">one</font>- to <font class="FactMarked mceNonEditable">four</font>-family residential loans, commercial real estate loans, multi-family real estate loans, home equity lines of credit and, to a much lesser extent, commercial business loans, construction loans and consumer loans. In the past we have also made land loans, and we may determine to resume making such loans in the future. At December</font><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">&nbsp;</font><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;"><font class="FactMarked mceNonEditable">31</font>, <font class="FactMarked mceNonEditable">2016</font>, our gross loans totaled $<font class="FactMarked Linked mceNonEditable">63.3</font> million, of which $<font class="FactMarked Linked mceNonEditable">30.3</font> million, or <font class="FactMarked Linked mceNonEditable">47.9</font>%, were <font class="FactMarked mceNonEditable">one</font>- to <font class="FactMarked mceNonEditable">four</font>-family residential loans, $<font class="FactMarked Linked mceNonEditable">25.3</font> million, or <font class="FactMarked Linked mceNonEditable">40.0</font>%, were multi-family residential and commercial real estate loans, and $<font class="FactMarked Linked mceNonEditable">5.4</font> million, or <font class="FactMarked Linked mceNonEditable">8.5</font>%, were home equity lines of credit. </font></p>

<p style="margin: 0pt;"><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 8pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin: 0pt; text-indent: 8%;"><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">Our loan portfolio has decreased from $109.8 million at December 31, 2008 to $62.3 million at December 31, 2016 primarily <font class="FactMarked mceNonEditable">due</font> to the effects of the severe economic recession that began in <font class="FactMarked mceNonEditable">2008</font>, and the related negative impact on our real estate market. During the economic downturn, we experienced higher non-performing assets and losses during the subsequent years. We are currently subject to a Consent Order with the Office of the Comptroller of the Currency which imposes certain minimum regulatory capital ratios which has required that we shrink our balance sheet to maintain adequate capital levels. Our current strategy is to increase our loan portfolio, especially our portfolio of commercial and multi-family real estate loans, and to a lesser extent commercial business loans, to increase our interest income and return to profitability. &nbsp;The successful implementation of our business strategy may require that we raise additional capital to maintain those minimums capital requirements as we gradually return to profitability. &nbsp;Such capital may not be available on terms that allow us to successfully implement our plan.</font></p>
<p style="margin: 0pt; text-indent: 8%;"><br></p>
<p style="margin: 0pt; text-indent: 8%;"><font><font style="font-family: 'times new roman', times; font-size: 10pt;">During 2016, the Bank experienced a number of personnel changes within the lending department that impacted our ability to generate the loan origination levels in our business plan.<font style="mso-spacerun: yes;">&nbsp; </font>The changes included the departure of our primary lending officer and his subsequent replacement several months later.<font style="mso-spacerun: yes;">&nbsp;&nbsp; </font>This position is primarily responsible for our residential lending portfolio and fee generation through originations for other institutions.<font style="mso-spacerun: yes;">&nbsp; </font>At the end of October 2016, we hired a senior loan officer to assume the Chief Lending Officer position.<font style="mso-spacerun: yes;">&nbsp; </font>This function had been the responsibility of the Bank&#8217;s President.<font style="mso-spacerun: yes;">&nbsp; </font>The new Chief Lending Officer is responsible for implementing strategies to attain our loan origination goals as well as overseeing our credit and loan administration functions.<font style="mso-spacerun: yes;">&nbsp; </font>Prior to accepting this position, this individual provided loan consulting service to the Bank since March of 2016. We believe that our new loan department structure along with our other referral sources, will help us meet our future production goals.<font style="mso-spacerun: yes;">&nbsp;&nbsp;</font></font></font></p>
<p style="margin: 12pt 0pt 0pt; text-indent: 8%;"><font><font style="font-family: 'times new roman', times; font-size: 10pt;"><font class="selected">In order to achieve profitability, our business plan anticipates growth in our <font class="FactMarked mceNonEditable">one</font>- to <font class="FactMarked mceNonEditable">four</font>-family residential, commercial real estate, and multi-family residential loan portfolios. In the longer term, we may also seek to increase our commercial business lending. We plan to supplement our internal loan production with purchases of <font class="FactMarked mceNonEditable">one</font>- to <font class="FactMarked mceNonEditable">four</font>-family residential and multi-family real estate loans and participations subject to our underwriting criteria. Loan growth will be subject to regulatory and market conditions. See &#8220;Management&#8217;s Discussion and Analysis of Financial Condition and Results of Operations&#8212;Business Strategy.&#8221;</font></font></font><br></p>

Maturities are based on the final contractual payment date and do not reflect the effect of prepayments. </font></p>

<p style="margin: 12pt 0pt 0pt; text-indent: 8%;"><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt; font-style: italic; font-weight: bold;">Loan Approval Procedures and Authority</font><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt; font-weight: bold;">.</font><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">&nbsp;</font><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">Pursuant to federal law, the aggregate amount of loans that we are permitted to make to any <font class="FactMarked mceNonEditable">one</font> borrower or a group of related borrowers is generally limited to <font class="FactMarked mceNonEditable">15</font>% of Ben Franklin Bank&#8217;s unimpaired capital and surplus (<font class="FactMarked mceNonEditable">25</font>% if the amount in excess of <font class="FactMarked mceNonEditable">15</font>% is secured by &#8220;readily marketable collateral&#8221; or <font class="FactMarked mceNonEditable">30</font>% for certain residential development loans). At December</font><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">&nbsp;</font><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;"><font class="FactMarked mceNonEditable">31</font>, <font class="FactMarked mceNonEditable">2016</font>, based on the <font class="FactMarked mceNonEditable">15</font>% limitation, our loans-to-<font class="FactMarked mceNonEditable">one</font>-borrower limit was approximately $<font class="FactMarked mceNonEditable">1.3</font> million. On the same date, we had<font> <font class="ParaMarked mceNonEditable">four</font></font> borrowers with outstanding balances and or commitments in excess of this amount. These outstanding balances and or commitments were within the respective limits at the time they were originated. &nbsp;As of December</font><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">&nbsp;</font><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;"><font class="FactMarked mceNonEditable">31</font>, <font class="FactMarked mceNonEditable">2016</font>, the largest dollar amount outstanding to <font class="FactMarked mceNonEditable">one</font> borrower, or group of related borrowers, was $<font class="FactMarked mceNonEditable">1.4</font> million consisting of<font> <font class="ParaMarked mceNonEditable">two</font></font> loans, each secured by a commercial retail property which were performing in accordance with its terms at December</font><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">&nbsp;</font><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;"><font class="FactMarked mceNonEditable">31</font>, <font class="FactMarked mceNonEditable">2016</font>. &nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin: 12pt 0pt 0pt; text-indent: 8%;"><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">Our lending is subject to written underwriting standards and origination procedures. Decisions on formal loan applications or written credit requests (&#8220;loan applications&#8221;) are made on the basis of sufficiently detailed applications submitted by the prospective borrower and/or guarantor and property valuations (consistent with our real estate appraisal policy) prepared by outside independent licensed appraisers approved by our board of directors if secured by real estate or business assets. The loan applications are designed primarily to determine the borrower&#8217;s ability to repay the requested loan, and the more significant items on the application are verified through use of credit reports, financial statements, tax returns and/or confirmations. </font></p>
<p style="margin: 12pt 0pt 0pt; text-indent: 8%;"><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">Under our loan policy, the individual lender that is processing an application is responsible for ensuring that all documentation is obtained prior to the submission of the application for approval. Additionally, each recommendation is formally documented in writing, using a loan presentation format appropriate for the request type. This document must memorialize the recommendation by providing all factors which support the decision. An independent officer then performs a credit review of these materials and assesses whether the requested loan meets our underwriting guidelines. Upon satisfactory secondary review, the loan is then presented for approval by the committee which has sufficient lending authority. As a general rule, under our loan policy, we do not originate or purchase &#8220;subprime loans&#8221; (loans that are made with low down-payments to borrowers with weakened credit histories typically characterized by payment delinquencies, previous charge-offs, judgments, bankruptcies, or borrowers with questionable repayment capacity as evidenced by low credit scores or high debt-burden ratios), &#8220;Alt-A loans&#8221; (defined as loans having less than full documentation) or no document loans. When a loan application is recommended for approval with characteristics that demonstrate the potential for the loan being considered a subprime loan, the lender must provide compelling support as to why the funding of this loan is in the best interests of the Bank. Further, any policy exception on loans in excess of $<font class="FactMarked mceNonEditable">150,000</font> must be identified and thoroughly mitigated and approved by the Board prior to funding. </font></p>
<p style="margin: 12pt 0pt 0pt; text-indent: 8%;"><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">While our loan policy provides for individual lending authorities, our general practice is that all loans, regardless of size, are reviewed and approved by a loan committee possessing sufficient lending authority. We have <font class="FactMarked mceNonEditable">two</font> such loan committees; the Board Loan Committee and the Officers Loan Committee. The Board Loan Committee reviews all loan requests of $<font class="FactMarked mceNonEditable">500,000 </font>up to $<font class="FactMarked mceNonEditable">1.0</font>&nbsp;million and recommends for approval by the board all requests of $<font class="FactMarked mceNonEditable">1.0</font>&nbsp;million and greater. The Board Loan Committee also ratifies all loans approved by the Officer Loan Committee. &nbsp; The Officers Loan Committee reviews all loans, regardless of size and has approval authority for all loans under $<font class="FactMarked mceNonEditable">500,000</font>. The Board ratifies all loans approved by the Board Loan Committee and the Officer Loan Committees and approves all loans of $<font class="FactMarked mceNonEditable">150,000</font> and greater that contain policy exceptions. &nbsp;As per the loan policy, our senior lending officer has approval authority for real </font></p>
<p style="margin: 0pt;"><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 8pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin: 0pt;"><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 8pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin: 0pt;"><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">estate loans of up to $<font class="FactMarked mceNonEditable">350,000</font> and home equity loans of up to $<font class="FactMarked mceNonEditable">250,000</font>. Real estate loans and home equity loans above those amounts require the approval of our President or Chief Executive Officer. Our senior lending officer has approval authority for secured commercial loans up to $<font class="FactMarked mceNonEditable">300,000</font>, construction loans up to $<font class="FactMarked mceNonEditable">350,000</font> and secured consumer loans of up to $<font class="FactMarked mceNonEditable">250,000</font>. Secured commercial loans, construction loans and secured consumer loans above those amounts require approval of our President or Chief Executive Officer. Per our loan policy, our President and Chief Executive Officers have approval authority for real estate loans, home equity, secured commercial, secured consumer loans,&nbsp;and construction loans up to $<font class="FactMarked mceNonEditable">500,000</font> each. Loans of $<font class="FactMarked mceNonEditable">500,000</font> and greater require the approval of our Officers Loan Committee. &nbsp;Loans of $<font class="FactMarked mceNonEditable">1.0</font> million and greater require approval by our Board Loan Committee. In addition, all loans are ratified by our board of directors. Loans in excess of $<font class="FactMarked mceNonEditable">150,000</font> that are subject to policy exceptions require the approval of the full board of directors. </font></p>
<p style="margin: 12pt 0pt 0pt; text-indent: 8%;"><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">Generally, we require title insurance or abstracts on our mortgage loans as well as fire and extended coverage casualty insurance in amounts at least equal to the principal amount of the loan or the value of improvements on the property, depending on the type of loan. We also require flood insurance to protect the property securing our interest when the property is located in a flood plain. In addition, we require escrow for property taxes, insurance and flood insurance (where appropriate) on the majority of our real estate secured loans, particularly on conventional <font class="FactMarked mceNonEditable">one</font>- to <font class="FactMarked mceNonEditable">four</font>-family residential loans. </font></p>
<p style="margin: 12pt 0pt 0pt; text-indent: 8%;"><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt; font-style: italic; font-weight: bold;"><font class="FactMarked mceNonEditable">One</font>- to <font class="FactMarked mceNonEditable">Four</font>-Family Residential Real Estate Lending</font><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt; font-weight: bold;">.</font><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;"> At December</font><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">&nbsp;</font><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;"><font class="FactMarked mceNonEditable">31</font>, <font class="FactMarked mceNonEditable">2016</font>, $<font class="FactMarked Linked mceNonEditable">30.3</font> million, or <font class="FactMarked Linked mceNonEditable">47.9</font>% of our gross loan portfolio consisted of residential mortgage loans. Of these loans, $<font class="FactMarked mceNonEditable">23.4</font> million were secured by owner occupied <font class="FactMarked mceNonEditable">one</font>- to <font class="FactMarked mceNonEditable">four</font>-family residences, and $<font class="FactMarked mceNonEditable">6.9</font> million were non-owner occupied. Our average outstanding <font class="FactMarked mceNonEditable">one</font>- to <font class="FactMarked mceNonEditable">four</font>-family residential loan balance $<font class="FactMarked mceNonEditable">174,000</font> and our largest outstanding residential loan had a principal balance of $<font class="FactMarked mceNonEditable">1.1</font>&nbsp;million at December</font><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">&nbsp;</font><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;"><font class="FactMarked mceNonEditable">31</font>, <font class="FactMarked mceNonEditable">2016</font>. The vast majority of the residential loans we originate are secured by properties located in our market area. </font></p>
<p style="margin: 12pt 0pt 0pt; text-indent: 8%;"><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">We offer both adjustable-rate and fixed-rate <font class="FactMarked mceNonEditable">one</font>- to <font class="FactMarked mceNonEditable">four</font>-family residential loans. However, <font class="FactMarked mceNonEditable">due</font> to consumer demand in the current and prolonged low interest rate environment, a significant portion of our <font class="FactMarked mceNonEditable">one</font>- to <font class="FactMarked mceNonEditable">four</font>-family residential loan portfolio consists of fixed-rate loans with original terms in excess of <font class="FactMarked mceNonEditable">15</font> years. At December</font><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">&nbsp;</font><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;"><font class="FactMarked mceNonEditable">31</font>, <font class="FactMarked mceNonEditable">2016</font>, $<font class="FactMarked mceNonEditable">21.4</font> million, or <font class="FactMarked mceNonEditable">70.6</font>% of our <font class="FactMarked mceNonEditable">one</font>- to <font class="FactMarked mceNonEditable">four</font>-family residential loans had fixed rates of interest. Of such loans, $<font class="FactMarked mceNonEditable">7.6</font> million had original contractual maturities of <font class="FactMarked mceNonEditable">10</font> years or less, $<font class="FactMarked mceNonEditable">7.5</font> million had original contractual maturities between <font class="FactMarked mceNonEditable">10</font> and <font class="FactMarked mceNonEditable">20</font> years and $<font class="FactMarked mceNonEditable">6.3</font> million had original contractual maturities in excess of <font class="FactMarked mceNonEditable">21</font> years in our portfolio. </font></p>
<p style="margin: 12pt 0pt 0pt; text-indent: 8%;"><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">While borrower preference favors fixed rates for <font class="FactMarked mceNonEditable">one</font>- to <font class="FactMarked mceNonEditable">four</font>-family residential mortgage loans given the historically low market rates, we offer adjustable-rate and short- and medium-term <font class="FactMarked mceNonEditable">one</font>- to <font class="FactMarked mceNonEditable">four</font>-family residential loans to help meet our asset/liability objectives. Our current adjustable-rate mortgage loans carry interest rates which adjust annually at a margin (generally <font class="FactMarked mceNonEditable">275</font> to <font class="FactMarked mceNonEditable">295</font> basis points) over the yield on <font class="FactMarked mceNonEditable">one</font>-year U.S. Treasury securities. These adjustable-rate loans generally have a fixed rate for the first <font class="FactMarked mceNonEditable">3</font> to <font class="FactMarked mceNonEditable">7</font> years of the loan term. Such loans carry terms to maturity of up to <font class="FactMarked mceNonEditable">30</font> years. The adjustable-rate mortgage loans currently offered by us generally provide for a <font class="FactMarked mceNonEditable">200</font> basis point annual interest rate change cap and a lifetime cap of <font class="FactMarked mceNonEditable">500</font> to <font class="FactMarked mceNonEditable">600</font> basis points over the initial rate. The initial interest rate on such loans is often fixed for a period of up to <font class="FactMarked mceNonEditable">seven</font> years. We determine whether a borrower qualifies for an adjustable-rate mortgage loan in conformance with the underwriting guidelines set forth by Fannie Mae and Freddie Mac in the secondary mortgage market.</font></p>
<p style="margin: 12pt 0pt 0pt; text-indent: 8%;"><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">Although adjustable-rate mortgage loans may reduce to an extent our vulnerability to changes in market interest rates because they periodically reprice, as interest rates increase, the required payments <font class="FactMarked mceNonEditable">due</font> from the borrower also increase (subject to rate caps), increasing the potential for default by the borrower. At the same time, the marketability of the underlying collateral may be adversely affected by higher interest rates. Upward adjustments of the contractual interest rate are also limited by the maximum periodic and lifetime rate adjustments permitted by our loan documents. Also, many of our adjustable-rate <font class="FactMarked mceNonEditable">one</font>- to <font class="FactMarked mceNonEditable">four</font>-family residential loans have fixed rates of interest for an initial period of up to <font class="FactMarked mceNonEditable">seven</font> years. As a result, the effectiveness of adjustable-rate mortgage loans may be limited during periods of rapidly rising interest rates. At December</font><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">&nbsp;</font><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;"><font class="FactMarked mceNonEditable">31</font>, <font class="FactMarked mceNonEditable">2016</font>, $<font class="FactMarked mceNonEditable">8.9</font> million, or <font class="FactMarked mceNonEditable">29.4</font>% of our <font class="FactMarked mceNonEditable">one</font>- to <font class="FactMarked mceNonEditable">four</font>-family residential loans, had adjustable rates of interest. </font></p>
<p style="margin: 0pt;"><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 8pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<div style="page-break-before: always; font-size: 10pt; text-align: left;"><a href="#TOC"><font style="font-family: 'times new roman', times; font-size: 10pt;">Table of Contents</font></a></div>

<p style="margin: 0pt;"><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 8pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin: 0pt; text-indent: 8%;"><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">As an alternative to adjustable-rate mortgage loans, we offer a bi-weekly fixed rate mortgage product that is unique to our market. We are not currently aware of any local competitor offering a similar product. As this product requires <font class="FactMarked mceNonEditable">26</font> payments per year, or the equivalent of <font class="FactMarked mceNonEditable">13</font> monthly payments each year, there is an accelerated amortization. For example, on a <font class="FactMarked mceNonEditable">25</font> year bi-weekly mortgage, if paid on time, it will fully amortize within <font class="FactMarked mceNonEditable">21.7</font> years. We offer bi-weekly mortgages at customizable terms within terms of <font class="FactMarked mceNonEditable">15</font>, <font class="FactMarked mceNonEditable">20</font>, <font class="FactMarked mceNonEditable">25</font> and <font class="FactMarked mceNonEditable">30</font> years. </font></p>
<p style="margin: 12pt 0pt 0pt; text-indent: 8%;"><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">Our current bi-weekly rate mortgage loans carry fixed interest rates priced from <font class="FactMarked mceNonEditable">3.625</font>% to <font class="FactMarked mceNonEditable">4.625</font>% for terms ranging from <font class="FactMarked mceNonEditable">15</font>&nbsp;years to <font class="FactMarked mceNonEditable">30</font> years. &nbsp;Although this is not a secondary mortgage market product, we generally determine whether a borrower qualifies for a bi-weekly mortgage loan in conformance with the underwriting guidelines set forth by Fannie Mae and Freddie Mac. &nbsp;We recently discontinued offering bi-weekly loans for&nbsp;non-owner-occupied mortgages.</font></p>
<p style="margin: 12pt 0pt 0pt; text-indent: 8%;"><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">We evaluate both the borrower&#8217;s ability to make principal, interest and escrow payments and the value of the property that will secure the loan. We currently originate residential mortgage loans for our portfolio with loan-to-value ratios of up to <font class="FactMarked mceNonEditable">80</font>% for owner-occupied <font class="FactMarked mceNonEditable">one</font>- to <font class="FactMarked mceNonEditable">four</font>-family homes and up to <font class="FactMarked mceNonEditable">75</font>% for non-owner occupied homes. With private mortgage insurance, we will lend up to <font class="FactMarked mceNonEditable">95</font>% for owner-occupied loans to well-qualified borrowers. </font></p>
<p style="margin: 12pt 0pt 0pt; text-indent: 8%;"><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">We generally do not offer &#8220;interest only&#8221; mortgage loans on <font class="FactMarked mceNonEditable">one</font>- to <font class="FactMarked mceNonEditable">four</font>-family residential properties. We also do not offer loans that provide for negative amortization of principal, such as &#8220;Option ARM&#8221; loans. Option ARM loans allow the borrower to pay less than the interest owed on the loan, resulting in an increased principal balance during the life of the loan. </font></p>
<p style="margin: 12pt 0pt 0pt; text-indent: 8%;"><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">In the past, we have made construction loans to builders and developers for the construction of <font class="FactMarked mceNonEditable">one</font>- to <font class="FactMarked mceNonEditable">four</font>- and multi-family residential units and to individuals for the construction of their primary or secondary residence. Our constructions loans generally require that the property is under contract for sales upon completion. Although we have curtailed our construction lending during the last few years, we believe that construction and land development lending is consistent with our community bank strategy. Construction and land lending generally affords us an opportunity to receive higher origination and other loan fees. In addition, such loans are generally made for relatively short terms. Nevertheless, construction financing is generally considered to involve a higher degree of credit risk than longer-term financing on improved, owner-occupied real estate. Risk of loss on a construction loan depends largely upon the accuracy of the initial estimate of the value of the property at completion of construction compared to the estimated cost (including interest) of construction and other assumptions. If the estimate of construction cost is inaccurate, we may be required to advance funds beyond the amount originally committed in order to protect the value of the property. Additionally, if the estimate of value is inaccurate, we may be confronted with a project, when completed, with a value that is insufficient to ensure full repayment of the loan.</font></p>
<p style="margin: 12pt 0pt 0pt; text-indent: 8%;"><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">At December 31, 2016&nbsp;<font style="color: #000000; font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 13.3333px; font-style: normal; font-variant-ligatures: normal; font-variant-caps: normal; font-weight: normal; letter-spacing: normal; orphans: 2; text-align: start; text-indent: 8%; text-transform: none; white-space: normal; widows: 2; word-spacing: 0px; -webkit-text-stroke-width: 0px; background-color: #ffffff; display: inline !important; float: none;">we had a&nbsp;<font>one</font><font style="color: #000000; font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 13.3333px; font-style: normal; font-variant-ligatures: normal; font-variant-caps: normal; font-weight: normal; letter-spacing: normal; orphans: 2; text-align: start; text-indent: 8%; text-transform: none; white-space: normal; widows: 2; word-spacing: 0px; -webkit-text-stroke-width: 0px; background-color: #ffffff; display: inline !important; float: none;">- to </font><font>four</font><font style="color: #000000; font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 13.3333px; font-style: normal; font-variant-ligatures: normal; font-variant-caps: normal; font-weight: normal; letter-spacing: normal; orphans: 2; text-align: start; text-indent: 8%; text-transform: none; white-space: normal; widows: 2; word-spacing: 0px; -webkit-text-stroke-width: 0px; background-color: #ffffff; display: inline !important; float: none;">-family residential mortgage</font>&nbsp;loan with an outstanding balance of $726,000 which was 90</font><font style="color: #000000; font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 13.3333px; font-style: normal; font-variant-ligatures: normal; font-variant-caps: normal; font-weight: normal; letter-spacing: normal; orphans: 2; text-align: start; text-indent: 8%; text-transform: none; white-space: normal; widows: 2; word-spacing: 0px; -webkit-text-stroke-width: 0px; background-color: #ffffff; display: inline !important; float: none;"> days or more delinquent and in non-accrual status and one troubled debt restructuring with an outstanding balance of $61,000 that was in non-accrual status.</font></font></p>
<p style="margin: 12pt 0pt 0pt; text-indent: 8%;"><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt; font-style: italic; font-weight: bold;">Commercial Real Estate Lending</font><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt; font-weight: bold;">.</font><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">&nbsp;Our commercial real estate loan portfolio was $<font class="FactMarked Linked mceNonEditable">15.3</font> million at December 31, 2016 compared to $<font class="FactMarked Linked mceNonEditable">13.9</font> million at December 31, 2015. &nbsp;<font style="color: #000000; font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 13.3333px; font-style: normal; font-variant-ligatures: normal; font-variant-caps: normal; font-weight: normal; letter-spacing: normal; orphans: 2; text-align: start; text-indent: 8%; text-transform: none; white-space: normal; widows: 2; word-spacing: 0px; -webkit-text-stroke-width: 0px; background-color: #ffffff; display: inline !important; float: none;">Our efforts to increase this segment of the portfolio are primarily the result of the personnel changes in our lending department, referrals from external sources, and</font><font style="color: #000000; font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 13.3333px; font-style: normal; font-variant-ligatures: normal; font-variant-caps: normal; font-weight: normal; letter-spacing: normal; orphans: 2; text-align: start; text-indent: 8%; text-transform: none; white-space: normal; widows: 2; word-spacing: 0px; -webkit-text-stroke-width: 0px; background-color: #ffffff; display: inline !important; float: none;">&nbsp;expanded relationships with other financial institutions for participations in loans they originate as we implement </font></font><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">our strategic plan. See &#8220;Management&#8217;s Discussion and Analysis of Financial Condition and Results of Operations&#8212;Business Strategy.&#8221; </font></p>
<p style="margin: 12pt 0pt 0pt; text-indent: 8%;"><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">Our commercial real estate loans generally have a maximum term of <font class="FactMarked mceNonEditable">5</font> years and are subject to a balloon payment at maturity. The amortization period for these loans is typically <font class="FactMarked mceNonEditable">25</font> years or less. These loans have fixed rates of interest for the entire term. At maturity, the borrower, and if applicable, guarantor, and the collateral are subjected to underwriting and valuation reviews. If this review process still finds these loans to be satisfactory, they are extended for an additional period of <font class="FactMarked mceNonEditable">three</font> to <font class="FactMarked mceNonEditable">five</font> years. Renewal rates are tied to certain indices, including the relevant Constant Maturity Treasury Bill Index or prime, plus a margin. In 2016 we also introduced a ten year term loan with a fixed interest rate for the first five years and then an annual rate adjustment each year for the remaining five year term. &nbsp;The amortization term for these loans is generally 25 years or less subject to a balloon payment at maturity. &nbsp;The initial rate and subsequent rate adjustments are <font style="color: #000000; font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 13.3333px; font-style: normal; font-variant-ligatures: normal; font-variant-caps: normal; font-weight: normal; letter-spacing: normal; orphans: 2; text-align: start; text-indent: 8%; text-transform: none; white-space: normal; widows: 2; word-spacing: 0px; -webkit-text-stroke-width: 0px; background-color: #ffffff; display: inline !important; float: none;">tied to the relevant Constant Maturity Treasury Bill Index.&nbsp;</font>Commercial real estate loans are generally made in amounts of up to <font class="FactMarked mceNonEditable">80</font>% of the lesser of the appraised value or the purchase price of the property with a projected debt service coverage ratio of at least <font class="FactMarked mceNonEditable">120</font>%. Most of our commercial real estate loans have principal balances less than $<font class="FactMarked mceNonEditable">1.0</font> million and include penalties for early repayment. </font></p>

<p style="margin: 0pt;"><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 8pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin: 0pt; text-indent: 8%;"><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">We consider a number of factors in originating commercial real estate loans. We evaluate the qualifications and financial condition of the borrower and/or guarantor, including their credit history, profitability and expertise, as well as the value and condition of the mortgaged property securing the loan. When evaluating the qualifications of the borrower and/or guarantor, we consider their financial resources, their debt to income and global debt service coverage ratios, their ability to provide outside support through income sources unrelated to the income producing property, their experience in owning or managing similar property and their payment history with us and other financial institutions. In evaluating the property securing the loan, the factors we consider include the net operating income of the mortgaged property before debt service and depreciation, the ratio of the loan amount to the appraised value of the mortgaged property, the condition of the property and the debt service coverage ratio (the ratio of net operating income to debt service) to assess whether it is at least <font class="FactMarked mceNonEditable">120</font>% of the monthly debt service. All commercial real estate loans are appraised by outside independent appraisers approved by the board of directors. Appraisals on all loans equal to or greater than $<font class="FactMarked mceNonEditable">500,000</font> or considered complex are reviewed by outside, independent third party review appraisers. All other appraisals are reviewed by <font class="FactMarked mceNonEditable">one</font> of our lenders or credit analysts who are independent of the transaction. Where the borrower is not an individual (such as a C or S corporation, limited liability company, partnership or land trust or other shell entity), we generally require personal guarantees on these loans.</font></p>
<p style="margin: 0pt; text-indent: 8%;"><br></p>
<p style="margin: 0pt; text-indent: 8%;"><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;"><font style="color: #000000; font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 13.3333px; font-style: normal; font-variant-ligatures: normal; font-variant-caps: normal; font-weight: normal; letter-spacing: normal; orphans: 2; text-align: start; text-indent: 8%; text-transform: none; white-space: normal; widows: 2; word-spacing: 0px; -webkit-text-stroke-width: 0px; background-color: #ffffff; display: inline !important; float: none;">The borrower&#8217;s financial information on commercial real estate loans is monitored on an ongoing basis by requiring periodic financial statement updates, payment history reviews, periodic face-to-face meetings, and site visits. We require such borrowers to provide annually updated financial statements and federal tax returns. These requirements also apply to the guarantors and/or principals of our corporate borrowers. We also require borrowers with rental investment property to provide an annual report of income and expenses for the property, including rent rolls/tenant lists, copies of leases and other information, as applicable.</font></font></p>
<p style="margin: 12pt 0pt 0pt; text-indent: 8%;"><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">Loans secured by commercial real estate generally are larger than <font class="FactMarked mceNonEditable">one</font>- to <font class="FactMarked mceNonEditable">four</font>-family residential loans and involve greater credit risk. Commercial real estate loans often involve large loan balances to single borrowers or groups of related borrowers. Repayment of these loans depends to a large degree on the results of operations and management of the properties securing the loans or the businesses conducted on such property, and may be affected to a greater extent by adverse conditions in the real estate market or the economy in general. Accordingly, the nature of these loans makes them more difficult for management to monitor and evaluate. At December</font><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">&nbsp;</font><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;"><font class="FactMarked mceNonEditable">31</font>, <font class="FactMarked mceNonEditable">2016</font>, we had one commercial real estate loan with an outstanding balance of $542,000 which was&nbsp;<font class="FactMarked mceNonEditable">90</font> days or more delinquent and in non-accrual status. </font></p>
<p style="margin: 12pt 0pt 0pt; text-indent: 8%;"><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">At December</font><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">&nbsp;</font><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;"><font class="FactMarked mceNonEditable">31</font>, <font class="FactMarked mceNonEditable">2016</font>, our largest commercial real estate loan totaled $1.3 million and was secured by an owner/user single occupant retail appliance store. At December</font><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">&nbsp;</font><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;"><font class="FactMarked mceNonEditable">31</font>, <font class="FactMarked mceNonEditable">2016</font>, this loan was performing in accordance with its terms. </font></p>
<p style="margin: 12pt 0pt 0pt; text-indent: 8%;"><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt; font-style: italic; font-weight: bold;">Multi-Family Real Estate Lending</font><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt; font-weight: bold;">.</font><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;"> At December</font><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">&nbsp;</font><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;"><font class="FactMarked mceNonEditable">31</font>, <font class="FactMarked mceNonEditable">2016</font>, we had multi-family real estate loans of $<font class="FactMarked Linked mceNonEditable">10.0</font> million compared to $<font class="FactMarked Linked mceNonEditable">7.6</font> million at December</font><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">&nbsp;</font><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;"><font class="FactMarked mceNonEditable">31</font>, <font class="FactMarked mceNonEditable">2015</font>. Our efforts to increase this segment of the portfolio are primarily the result of personnel changes in our lending department, referrals from external sources, and&nbsp;expanded relationships with other financial institutions for participations in loans they originate <font style="color: #000000; font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 13.3333px; font-style: normal; font-variant-ligatures: normal; font-variant-caps: normal; font-weight: normal; letter-spacing: normal; orphans: 2; text-align: start; text-indent: 8%; text-transform: none; white-space: normal; widows: 2; word-spacing: 0px; -webkit-text-stroke-width: 0px; background-color: #ffffff; display: inline !important; float: none;">as we implement </font><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">our strategic plan.</font>&nbsp;See &#8220;Management&#8217;s Discussion and Analysis of Financial Condition and Results of Operations&#8212;Business Strategy.&#8221; </font></p>
<p style="margin: 12pt 0pt 0pt; text-indent: 8%;"><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">The multi-family real estate loans we originate generally have a maximum term of <font class="FactMarked mceNonEditable">five</font> years and are subject to balloon payments at maturity. <font style="color: #000000; font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 13.3333px; font-style: normal; font-variant-ligatures: normal; font-variant-caps: normal; font-weight: normal; letter-spacing: normal; orphans: 2; text-align: start; text-indent: 8%; text-transform: none; white-space: normal; widows: 2; word-spacing: 0px; -webkit-text-stroke-width: 0px; background-color: #ffffff; display: inline !important; float: none;">The amortization period for these loans is typically </font><font>25</font><font style="color: #000000; font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 13.3333px; font-style: normal; font-variant-ligatures: normal; font-variant-caps: normal; font-weight: normal; letter-spacing: normal; orphans: 2; text-align: start; text-indent: 8%; text-transform: none; white-space: normal; widows: 2; word-spacing: 0px; -webkit-text-stroke-width: 0px; background-color: #ffffff; display: inline !important; float: none;"> years or less.&nbsp;</font>The interest rates on these loans are generally fixed for the entire term. <font style="color: #000000; font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 13.3333px; font-style: normal; font-variant-ligatures: normal; font-variant-caps: normal; font-weight: normal; letter-spacing: normal; orphans: 2; text-align: start; text-indent: 8%; text-transform: none; white-space: normal; widows: 2; word-spacing: 0px; -webkit-text-stroke-width: 0px; background-color: #ffffff; display: inline !important; float: none;"> At maturity, the borrower, and if applicable, guarantor, and the collateral are subjected to underwriting and valuation reviews. &nbsp;If this review process still finds these loans to be satisfactory, they are extended for an additional period of </font><font>three</font><font style="color: #000000; font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 13.3333px; font-style: normal; font-variant-ligatures: normal; font-variant-caps: normal; font-weight: normal; letter-spacing: normal; orphans: 2; text-align: start; text-indent: 8%; text-transform: none; white-space: normal; widows: 2; word-spacing: 0px; -webkit-text-stroke-width: 0px; background-color: #ffffff; display: inline !important; float: none;"> to </font><font>five</font><font style="color: #000000; font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 13.3333px; font-style: normal; font-variant-ligatures: normal; font-variant-caps: normal; font-weight: normal; letter-spacing: normal; orphans: 2; text-align: start; text-indent: 8%; text-transform: none; white-space: normal; widows: 2; word-spacing: 0px; -webkit-text-stroke-width: 0px; background-color: #ffffff; display: inline !important; float: none;"> years. &nbsp;</font>Should the loan be renewed at maturity, the rates are adjusted to current market rates and the loan is extended for an additional <font class="FactMarked mceNonEditable">three</font> to <font class="FactMarked mceNonEditable">five</font> years.<font style="color: #000000; font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 13.3333px; font-style: normal; font-variant-ligatures: normal; font-variant-caps: normal; font-weight: normal; letter-spacing: normal; orphans: 2; text-align: start; text-indent: 8%; text-transform: none; white-space: normal; widows: 2; word-spacing: 0px; -webkit-text-stroke-width: 0px; background-color: #ffffff; display: inline !important; float: none;"> Renewal rates are tied to certain indices, including the relevant Constant Maturity Treasury Bill Index or prime, plus a margin.</font>&nbsp; <font style="color: #000000; font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 13.3333px; font-style: normal; font-variant-ligatures: normal; font-variant-caps: normal; font-weight: normal; letter-spacing: normal; orphans: 2; text-align: start; text-indent: 8%; text-transform: none; white-space: normal; widows: 2; word-spacing: 0px; -webkit-text-stroke-width: 0px; background-color: #ffffff; display: inline !important; float: none;">In 2016, we also introduced a ten year term loan with a fixed interest rate for the first five years and then an annual rate adjustment each year for the remaining five year term. &nbsp;The amortization term for these loans is generally 25 years or less subject to a balloon payment at maturity. &nbsp;The initial rate and subsequent rate adjustments are </font><font style="color: #000000; font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 13.3333px; font-style: normal; font-variant-ligatures: normal; font-variant-caps: normal; font-weight: normal; letter-spacing: normal; orphans: 2; text-align: start; font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 13.3333px; font-style: normal; font-variant-ligatures: normal; font-variant-caps: normal; font-weight: normal; letter-spacing: normal; orphans: 2; text-align: start; text-indent: 8%; text-transform: none; white-space: normal; widows: 2; word-spacing: 0px; -webkit-text-stroke-width: 0px; background-color: #ffffff; display: inline !important; float: none;">&nbsp;</font>Most of our multi-family loans have principal balances less than $<font class="FactMarked mceNonEditable">1.0</font> million and include penalties for early repayment.&nbsp;Our multi-family real estate loans are secured by apartment buildings located within the greater Chicago area.</font></p>
<p style="margin: 12pt 0pt 0pt; text-indent: 8%;"><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">Appraisals on properties securing multi-family real estate loans are performed by an outside independent appraiser designated by us at the time the loan is made. All appraisals on multi-family real estate loans are reviewed. Appraisals on all loans equal to or greater than $<font class="FactMarked mceNonEditable">500,000</font> or considered complex are reviewed by outside, independent third party review appraisers. All other appraisals are reviewed by <font class="FactMarked mceNonEditable">one</font> of our lenders <font style="color: #000000; font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 13.3333px; font-style: normal; font-variant-ligatures: normal; font-variant-caps: normal; font-weight: normal; letter-spacing: normal; orphans: 2; text-align: start; text-indent: 8%; text-transform: none; white-space: normal; widows: 2; word-spacing: 0px; -webkit-text-stroke-width: 0px; background-color: #ffffff; display: inline !important; float: none;"> or credit analysts&nbsp;</font>who are independent of the transaction. Our underwriting procedures include considering the borrower&#8217;s and/or the guarantor&#8217;s expertise and require verification of their credit history, sources of income and financial statements, banking relationships, references and income projections for the property. Where the borrower is not an individual (such as a C or S corporation, limited liability company, partnership or land trust or other shell entity), we generally require personal guarantees on these loans. </font></p>

<p style="margin: 0pt;"><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 8pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin: 0pt; text-indent: 8%;"><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">The borrower&#8217;s financial information on multi-family loans is monitored on an ongoing basis by requiring periodic financial statement updates, payment history reviews, periodic face-to-face meetings, and site visits. We require such borrowers to provide annually updated financial statements and federal tax returns. These requirements also apply to the guarantors and/or principals of our corporate borrowers. We also require borrowers with rental investment property to provide an annual report of income and expenses for the property, including rent rolls/tenant lists, copies of leases and other information, as applicable. </font></p>
<p style="margin: 12pt 0pt 0pt; text-indent: 8%;"><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">Multi-family real estate loans generally present a higher level of risk than loans secured by <font class="FactMarked mceNonEditable">one</font>- to <font class="FactMarked mceNonEditable">four</font>-family residences. This greater risk is <font class="FactMarked mceNonEditable">due</font> to several factors, including the concentration of principal in a limited number of loans and borrowers, the effects of general economic conditions on income-producing properties and the increased difficulty of evaluating and monitoring these types of loans. Furthermore, the repayment of loans secured by multi-family residential real estate is typically dependent upon the successful operation of the related real estate project. If the cash flow from the project is reduced (for example, if leases are not obtained or renewed), the borrower&#8217;s ability to repay the loan may be impaired. At December</font><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">&nbsp;</font><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;"><font class="FactMarked mceNonEditable">31</font>, <font class="FactMarked mceNonEditable">2016</font>, we had <font class="FactMarked mceNonEditable">one</font> multi-family real estate loan with an aggregate outstanding balance of $<font><font style="/* background-color: #a5e3d1;"><font class="FactMarked Linked mceNonEditable">284,000</font></font></font>&nbsp;which was in non-accrual status. </font></p>
<p style="margin: 12pt 0pt 0pt; text-indent: 8%;"><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">At December</font><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">&nbsp;</font><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;"><font class="FactMarked mceNonEditable">31</font>, <font class="FactMarked mceNonEditable">2016</font>, our largest multi-family loan had a balance of $<font class="FactMarked mceNonEditable">891,000</font>&nbsp;and was a secured by <font class="FactMarked mceNonEditable">two</font>&nbsp;apartment buildings with a total of <font class="FactMarked mceNonEditable">24</font> units. At December</font><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">&nbsp;</font><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;"><font class="FactMarked mceNonEditable">31</font>, <font class="FactMarked mceNonEditable">2016</font>, this loan was performing in accordance with its terms and subsequently was paid off in February of <font class="FactMarked mceNonEditable">2017</font>. </font></p>
<p style="margin: 12pt 0pt 0pt; text-indent: 8%;"><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt; font-style: italic; font-weight: bold;">Home Equity Lending. </font><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">We originate variable-rate home equity lines of credit and, to a lesser extent, fixed- and variable-rate loans secured by a lien on the borrower&#8217;s primary residence. Our home equity products are limited to <font class="FactMarked mceNonEditable">80</font>% of the property value less any other mortgages. </font></p>
<p style="margin: 12pt 0pt 0pt; text-indent: 8%;"><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">In 2016, we began offering a new home equity line product. &nbsp;The new structure combines a <font class="FactMarked mceNonEditable">10</font> year draw period with a 15 year (second lien) or 20 year (first lien) fully amortizing loan. &nbsp;At the tenth anniversary of the date of funding, the outstanding balance at that time will automatically convert to the fully amortizing structure. This&nbsp;<font style="color: #000000; font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 13.3333px; font-style: normal; font-variant-ligatures: normal; font-variant-caps: normal; font-weight: normal; letter-spacing: normal; orphans: 2; text-align: start; text-indent: 8%; text-transform: none; white-space: normal; widows: 2; word-spacing: 0px; -webkit-text-stroke-width: 0px; background-color: #ffffff; display: inline !important; float: none;">product carries an interest rate tied to the prime rate published in the Wall Street Journal for the entire term of the loan with a margin that ranges from prime to prime minus </font><font class="FactMarked mceNonEditable">100</font><font style="color: #000000; font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 13.3333px; font-style: normal; font-variant-ligatures: normal; font-variant-caps: normal; font-weight: normal; letter-spacing: normal; orphans: 2; text-align: start; text-indent: 8%; text-transform: none; white-space: normal; widows: 2; word-spacing: 0px; -webkit-text-stroke-width: 0px; background-color: #ffffff; display: inline !important; float: none;"> basis points and a floor of 3.50% for first lien loans and a margin that ranges from prime to prime minus 50&nbsp;<font style="color: #000000; font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 13.3333px; font-style: normal; font-variant-ligatures: normal; font-variant-caps: normal; font-weight: normal; letter-spacing: normal; orphans: 2; text-align: start; text-indent: 8%; text-transform: none; white-space: normal; widows: 2; word-spacing: 0px; -webkit-text-stroke-width: 0px; background-color: #ffffff; display: inline !important; float: none;">basis points and a floor of 4.00% for second lien loans.</font>&nbsp; The product has a rate ceiling of&nbsp;</font><font class="FactMarked mceNonEditable">17.5</font><font style="color: #000000; font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 13.3333px; font-style: normal; font-variant-ligatures: normal; font-variant-caps: normal; font-weight: normal; letter-spacing: normal; orphans: 2; text-align: start; text-indent: 8%; text-transform: none; white-space: normal; widows: 2; word-spacing: 0px; -webkit-text-stroke-width: 0px; background-color: #ffffff; display: inline !important; float: none;">%. </font><font style="color: #000000; font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 13.3333px; font-style: normal; font-variant-ligatures: normal; font-variant-caps: normal; font-weight: normal; letter-spacing: normal; orphans: 2; text-align: start; text-indent: 8%; text-transform: none; white-space: normal; widows: 2; word-spacing: 0px; -webkit-text-stroke-width: 0px; background-color: #ffffff; display: inline !important; float: none;">&nbsp;A prepayment penalty is assessed if the line is closed within </font><font class="FactMarked mceNonEditable">one</font><font style="color: #000000; font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 13.3333px; font-style: normal; font-variant-ligatures: normal; font-variant-caps: normal; font-weight: normal; letter-spacing: normal; orphans: 2; text-align: start; text-indent: 8%; text-transform: none; white-space: normal; widows: 2; word-spacing: 0px; -webkit-text-stroke-width: 0px; background-color: #ffffff; display: inline !important; float: none;"> year.</font></font></p>
<p style="margin: 12pt 0pt 0pt; text-indent: 8%;"><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">We continue to offer a&nbsp;<font class="FactMarked mceNonEditable">seven</font>-year balloon home equity line of credit product, meaning the entire balance is <font class="FactMarked mceNonEditable">due</font> at maturity. To determine the pro forma payment at the end of the original term for underwriting purposes, we assume the commitment is fully drawn and we use a <font class="FactMarked mceNonEditable">2.0</font>% shock over the current rate and amortize the loan over a <font class="FactMarked mceNonEditable">seven</font> year term. This product carries an interest rate tied to the prime rate published in the Wall Street Journal with a margin that ranges from prime to prime minus <font>125</font> basis points. The product has a rate ceiling of&nbsp;<font>17.5</font>% and a floor of&nbsp;<font class="FactMarked mceNonEditable">4.00</font>% for first lien position loans and <font class="FactMarked mceNonEditable">5.00</font>% for second lien position loans. A prepayment penalty is assessed if the line is closed within <font>one</font> year. </font></p>
<p style="margin: 12pt 0pt 0pt; text-indent: 8%;"><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">We currently also offer fixed rate fully amortizing home equity loans with a term of&nbsp;<font class="FactMarked mceNonEditable">five</font>&nbsp;years. We use the same underwriting standards for home equity loans as we use for one- to <font class="FactMarked mceNonEditable">four</font>-family residential mortgage loans. Our current home equity loan product carries an interest rate of <font class="FactMarked mceNonEditable">6.00</font>% with no origination fees or <font class="FactMarked mceNonEditable">5.00</font>% with a <font class="FactMarked mceNonEditable">1.00</font>% fee. We discontinued offering fixed rate home equity loans subject to balloon payments.&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin: 0pt;"><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 8pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin: 0pt;"><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 8pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin: 0pt; text-indent: 8%;"><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">At December</font><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">&nbsp;</font><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;"><font class="FactMarked mceNonEditable">31</font>, <font class="FactMarked mceNonEditable">2016</font>, we had $<font class="FactMarked Linked mceNonEditable">5.4</font> million, or <font class="FactMarked Linked mceNonEditable">8.5</font>%, of gross loans in home equity loans and outstanding advances under home equity lines of credit and an additional $<font class="FactMarked mceNonEditable">5.0</font> million of funds committed, but not advanced, under home equity lines of credit. &nbsp;At December 31, 2016, we had one loan with an outstanding balance of $241,000 that was in non-accrual status.</font></p>
<p style="margin: 12pt 0pt 0pt; text-indent: 8%;"><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt; font-style: italic; font-weight: bold;">Commercial Business Loans</font><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt; font-weight: bold;">.</font><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;"> We originate or purchase secured or unsecured loans to professionals, sole proprietorships and small businesses for commercial, corporate and business purposes. Commercial business lending products include term loans, revolving lines of credit and leases. We also may make commercial business loans under certain programs of the U.S. Small Business Administration. Our commercial business loans are generally used for working capital purposes or for acquiring equipment, inventory or furniture. </font></p>
<p style="margin: 12pt 0pt 0pt; text-indent: 8%;"><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">Our commercial business loans totaled </font><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">$<font class="FactMarked Linked mceNonEditable">1.2</font> million at December 31, 2016. &nbsp;We have a relationship with a private lending firm from which we purchase individual loans to medical practitioners for financing medical equipment and for working capital for establishing private practices. These loans are treated as a loan to <font class="FactMarked mceNonEditable">one</font> borrower, as the originating firm can replace any loan that is not performing as agreed with another performing loan from its own captive portfolio. We focus on the private lender as our primary source of repayment and require annual financial updates. At December</font><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">&nbsp;</font><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;"><font class="FactMarked mceNonEditable">31</font>, <font class="FactMarked mceNonEditable">2016</font>, there were <font class="FactMarked mceNonEditable">19</font> loans purchased from this firm that made up $<font class="FactMarked mceNonEditable">1.2</font></font><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">&nbsp;</font><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">million, or <font class="FactMarked mceNonEditable">99.0</font>%, of our commercial loan portfolio. None of the loans purchased from this source have defaulted. We expect that we will continue this line of lending in the future. </font></p>
<p style="margin: 12pt 0pt 0pt; text-indent: 8%;"><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">When making commercial business loans, we consider the financial statements of the borrower, the lending history of the borrower, the debt service capabilities of the borrower, the projected cash flows of the business, the value of the collateral, if any, and whether the loan is guaranteed by the principals of the borrower. Commercial business loans are generally secured by accounts receivable, inventory, equipment and/or real estate. Depending on the amount of the loan and the collateral used to secure the loan, commercial business loans are made in amounts of up to <font class="FactMarked mceNonEditable">75</font>% of the value of the collateral securing the loan. Commercial business loans are made with terms usually less than <font class="FactMarked mceNonEditable">five</font> years with either variable or fixed rates of interest. Variable rates are based on the prime rate plus a margin. Fixed-rate commercial business loans are set at a margin above prime rate. </font></p>
<p style="margin: 12pt 0pt 0pt; text-indent: 8%;"><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">Commercial business loans generally have a greater credit risk than residential mortgage loans. Unlike residential mortgage loans, which generally are made on the basis of the borrower&#8217;s ability to make repayment from his or her employment and other income, and which are secured by real property whose value tends to be more easily ascertainable, commercial business loans are of higher risk and typically are made on the basis of the borrower&#8217;s ability to make repayment from the cash flow of the borrower&#8217;s business. As a result, the availability of funds for the repayment of commercial business loans may be substantially dependent on the success of the business itself. Further, the collateral securing the loans may depreciate over time, may be difficult to appraise and may fluctuate in value based on the success of the business. We seek to minimize these risks through our underwriting standards. </font></p>
<p style="margin: 12pt 0pt 0pt; text-indent: 8%;"><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">At December</font><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">&nbsp;</font><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;"><font class="FactMarked mceNonEditable">31</font>, <font class="FactMarked mceNonEditable">2016</font>, our largest commercial business loan relationship was the aforementioned private lending firm&#8217;s loans to medical practitioners with a balance of $<font class="FactMarked mceNonEditable">1.2</font> million. At December</font><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">&nbsp;</font><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;"><font class="FactMarked mceNonEditable">31</font>, <font class="FactMarked mceNonEditable">2016</font>, these loans were performing in accordance with their original terms. </font></p>
<p style="margin: 12pt 0pt 0pt; text-indent: 8%;"><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt; font-style: italic; font-weight: bold;">Consumer Lending</font><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">. In the past we purchased&nbsp;<font style="color: #000000; font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 13.3333px; font-style: normal; font-variant-ligatures: normal; font-variant-caps: normal; font-weight: normal; letter-spacing: normal; orphans: 2; text-align: start; text-indent: 8%; text-transform: none; white-space: normal; widows: 2; word-spacing: 0px; -webkit-text-stroke-width: 0px; background-color: #ffffff; display: inline !important; float: none;">new and used automobiles</font>&nbsp;under an agreement with a local bank to diversify our portfolio and increase our interest income. &nbsp;</font><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">In January 2014, we suspended new purchases under this agreement based on the review of risk concentrations in our portfolio, liquidity requirements, and economic conditions. Between December</font><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">&nbsp;</font><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;"><font class="FactMarked mceNonEditable">31</font>, <font class="FactMarked mceNonEditable">2009</font> and December</font><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">&nbsp;</font><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;"><font class="FactMarked mceNonEditable">31</font>, <font class="FactMarked mceNonEditable">2016</font>, purchased automobile loans decreased from $<font class="FactMarked mceNonEditable">7.2</font> million to $<font class="FactMarked mceNonEditable">357,000</font>. At this time we do not anticipate the resumption of the automobile purchase program.</font></p>
<p style="margin: 12pt 0pt 0pt; text-indent: 8%;"><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">We also offer consumer loans directly to customers in our market area with acceptable credit ratings. At December</font><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">&nbsp;</font><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;"><font class="FactMarked mceNonEditable">31</font>, <font class="FactMarked mceNonEditable">2016</font>, we had $14,000 of consumer loans other than automobile loans. </font></p>
<p style="margin: 0pt;"><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 8pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
