<p style="margin: 0pt; text-align: center;"><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">BEN FRANKLIN FINANCIAL, INC. </font></p>
<p style="margin: 0pt; text-align: center;"><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">NOTES TO CONSOLIDATED FINANCIAL STATEMENTS </font></p>
<p style="margin: 0pt; text-align: center;"><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">As of and for the Years Ended December 31, 2016 and <font style="border-left: none; border-right: none;">2015</font></font></p>
<p style="margin: 0pt; text-align: center;"><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">(Dollars in thousands except per share data) </font></p>
<p style="margin: 0pt 0pt 2pt; line-height: 12pt; border-bottom-color: #000000; border-bottom-width: 0.75pt; border-bottom-style: solid;"><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 12pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin: 0pt;"><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 8pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin: 0pt;"><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt; font-weight: bold;">NOTE <font style="border-left: none; border-right: none;">1</font> - SUMMARY OF SIGNIFICANT ACCOUNTING POLICIES </font><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">(Continued)</font><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt; font-weight: bold;"> </font></p>
</div>
<p style="margin: 0pt;"><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 8pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<div class="TaggedFact">
<div>
<p style="margin: 0pt;"><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt; text-decoration: underline;">Operating Segments</font><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">: <font style="font-family: 'times new roman', times;">While the chief decision-makers monitor the revenue streams of the various products and services, operations are managed and financial performance is evaluated on a Company-wide basis. Operating segments are aggregated into <font class=" FactMarked">one</font>, as operating results for all segments are similar. Accordingly, all of the financial service operations are considered by management to be aggregated in <font class="TaggedFact">one</font> reportable operating segment.</font></font></p>
</div>
</div>
<p style="margin: 0pt;"><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<div class="TaggedFact">
<p style="margin: 0pt 0in 0in; font-size: 12pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman', serif;"><font style="font-family: 'times new roman', times; font-size: 10pt;"><font style="text-decoration: underline;">New Accounting Standards</font>:&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin: 0pt 0in 0in; font-size: 12pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman', serif;"><br></p>
<p style="margin: 0in 0in 0.0001pt; font-size: 11pt; font-family: Calibri, sans-serif;"><font style="font-family: 'times new roman', times; font-size: 10pt;"><font><font>In August 2014, the FASB released ASU 2014-15, Presentation of Financial Statements-Going Concern (Subtopic 205-40): Disclosure of Uncertainties About an Entity&#8217;s Ability to Continue as a Going Concern which amended existing guidance related to the disclosures about an entity&#8217;s ability to continue as a going concern. These amendments are intended to define management&#8217;s responsibility to evaluate whether there is substantial doubt about an organization&#8217;s ability to continue as a going concern and to provide related footnote disclosures. These amendments provide guidance to an organization&#8217;s management, with principles and definitions that are intended to reduce diversity in the timing and content of disclosures that are commonly provided by organizations in the financial statement footnotes.&nbsp; The amendments are effective for annual periods ending after December 15, 2016, and interim periods within annual periods beginning after December 15, 2016.&nbsp;&nbsp; The adoption of this standard did not have a material effect on the Company&#8217;s operating results or financial condition.</font></font><i></i></font></p>
<p style="margin: 0pt 0in 0in; font-size: 12pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman', serif;"><br></p>
<p style="margin: 0pt 0in 0in; font-size: 12pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman', serif;"><font style="font-family: 'times new roman', times; font-size: 10pt;">In January 2016 the FASB released accounting standards update 2016-01 Recognition and Measurement of Financial Assets and Liabilities. The main provisions of the update are to eliminate the available for sale classification of accounting for equity securities and to adjust the fair value disclosures for financial instruments carried at amortized costs such that the disclosed fair values represent an exit price as opposed to an entry price. The provisions of this update will require that equity securities be carried at fair market value on the balance sheet and any periodic changes in value will be adjustments to the income statement. A practical expedient is provided for equity securities without a readily determinable fair value, such that these securities can be carried at cost less any impairment. The provisions of this update become effective for interim and annual periods beginning after December&nbsp;15,&nbsp;2017. Management does not expect the requirements of this update to have a material impact on the Company&#8217;s financial position, results of operations or cash flows.</font></p>
<p style="margin: 0pt;"><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin: 0pt 0in 0.0001pt; font-size: 12pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman', serif;"><font style="font-family: 'times new roman', times; font-size: 10pt;">In February 2016, the FASB issued accounting standards update 2016-02 Leases. The update requires all leases, with the exception of short-term leases that have contractual terms no greater than one year, to be recorded on the balance sheet. Under the provisions of the update, leases classified as operating will be reflected on the balance sheet with the recognition of both a right-of-use asset and a lease liability. Under the update, a distinction will exist between finance and operating type leases and the rules for determining which classification a lease will fall into are similar to existing rules. For public business entities, the amendments of this update are effective for interim and annual periods beginning after December&nbsp;15, 2018. The update requires a modified retrospective transition under which comparative balance sheets from the earliest historical period presented will be revised to reflect what the financials would have looked like were the provisions of the update applied consistently in all prior periods. Management has not yet determined the impacts of this update on the Company&#8217;s financial position, results of operations or cash flows. &nbsp;Based on lease commitments outstanding, we anticipate that total assets and liabilities will increase approximately $2.0 million.</font></p>
<p style="margin: 0pt;"><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin: 0pt 0in 0.0001pt; font-size: 12pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman', serif;"><font style="font-family: 'times new roman', times; font-size: 10pt;">In March 2016 the FASB issued accounting standards update 2016-09 Compensation-Stock Compensation. The purpose of the update was to simplify the accounting for share-based payment transactions, including the income tax consequences of such transactions. Under the provisions of the update the income tax consequences of excess tax benefits and deficiencies should be recognized in income tax expense in the reporting period in which the awards vest. Currently, excess tax benefits or deficiencies impact stockholders&#8217; equity directly to the extent there is a cumulative excess tax benefit. In the event that a tax deficiency has occurred during the reporting period and a cumulative excess tax benefit does not exist, the tax deficiency is recognized in income tax expense under current GAAP. The update also provides that entities may continue to estimate forfeitures in accounting for stock based compensation or recognize them as they occur. The provisions of this update become effective for interim and annual periods beginning after December&nbsp;15, 2016. Management does not expect the requirements of this update to have a material impact on the Company&#8217;s financial position, results of operations or cash flows. </font></p>

<p style="margin: 0pt; text-align: center;"><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">BEN FRANKLIN FINANCIAL, INC. </font></p>
<p style="margin: 0pt; text-align: center;"><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">NOTES TO CONSOLIDATED FINANCIAL STATEMENTS </font></p>
<p style="margin: 0pt; text-align: center;"><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">As of and for the Years Ended December 31, 2016 and <font style="border-left: none; border-right: none;">2015</font></font></p>
<p style="margin: 0pt; text-align: center;"><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">(Dollars in thousands except per share data) </font></p>
<p style="margin: 0pt 0pt 2pt; line-height: 12pt; border-bottom-color: #000000; border-bottom-width: 0.75pt; border-bottom-style: solid;"><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 12pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin: 0pt;"><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 8pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin: 0pt;"><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt; font-weight: bold;">NOTE <font style="border-left: none; border-right: none;">1</font> - SUMMARY OF SIGNIFICANT ACCOUNTING POLICIES </font><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">(Continued)</font><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt; font-weight: bold;"> </font></p>
</div>
<p style="margin: 0pt;"><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin: 0pt 0in 0.0001pt; font-size: 12pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman', serif;"><font style="font-family: 'times new roman', times; font-size: 10pt;">In June 2016 the FASB issued accounting standards update 2016-13 Measurement of Credit Losses on Financial Instruments. The main objective of this update is to provide financial statement users with more decision-useful information about the expected credit losses on financial instruments and other commitments to extend credit held by a reporting entity at each reporting date. To achieve this objective, the amendments in this update replace the incurred loss impairment methodology in current GAAP with a methodology that reflects expected credit losses and requires consideration of a broader range of reasonable and supportable information to inform credit loss estimates. The amendments affect entities holding financial assets and net investment in leases that are not accounted for at fair value through net income. The amendments affect loans, debt securities classified as held to maturity, trade receivables, net investments in leases, off-balance-sheet credit exposures, reinsurance receivables, and any other financial assets not excluded from the scope that have the contractual right to receive cash. The provisions of this update are effective for fiscal years beginning after December&nbsp;15, 2019, including interim periods within those fiscal years. Management has not yet determined the impacts of this update on the Company&#8217;s financial position, results of operations or cash flows.</font></p>
</div>
</div>
<p style="margin: 0pt;"><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">&nbsp;</font></p><div class="TaggedFact">
<p style="margin: 0pt;"><font style="color: #000000; font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 13.3333px; font-style: normal; font-variant-ligatures: normal; font-variant-caps: normal; font-weight: bold; letter-spacing: normal; orphans: 2; text-align: start; text-indent: 0px; text-transform: none; white-space: normal; widows: 2; word-spacing: 0px; -webkit-text-stroke-width: 0px; display: inline !important; float: none;">NOT</font><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 13.3333px; font-style: normal; font-variant-ligatures: normal; font-variant-caps: normal; font-weight: bold; letter-spacing: normal; orphans: 2; text-align: start; text-indent: 0px; text-transform: none; white-space: normal; widows: 2; word-spacing: 0px; -webkit-text-stroke-width: 0px; float: none; display: inline !important;">E </font><font style="font-family: 'times new roman', times; font-size: 10pt;"><strong><font style="border-left: none; border-right: none;">2</font></strong></font><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 13.3333px; font-style: normal; font-variant-ligatures: normal; font-variant-caps: normal; font-weight: bold; letter-spacing: normal; orphans: 2; text-align: start; text-indent: 0px; text-transform: none; white-space: normal; widows: 2; word-spacing: 0px; -webkit-text-stroke-width: 0px; float: none; display: inline !important;"> - REC</font><font style="color: #000000; font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 13.3333px; font-style: normal; font-variant-ligatures: normal; font-variant-caps: normal; font-weight: bold; letter-spacing: normal; orphans: 2; text-align: start; text-indent: 0px; text-transform: none; white-space: normal; widows: 2; word-spacing: 0px; -webkit-text-stroke-width: 0px; display: inline !important; float: none;">URRING LOSSES</font></p>
<p style="margin: 6pt 0pt 0pt;"><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">The Company has incurred losses since <font class=" FactMarked">2008</font>&nbsp;resulting from a combination of: declining net interest income, as our loan portfolio decreased from $<font class="TaggedFact">109.8</font> million at December 31, 2008 to $<font class=" FactMarked">62.3</font> million at December 31, 2016; increased provisions for loan losses between 2009 and 2012; and increasing non-interest expense related to professional fees and&nbsp;repossessed asset write-downs and costs. &nbsp;The Company recently incurred net losses of $<font class=" FactMarked">1,260</font>&nbsp;during the year ended December</font><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">&nbsp;</font><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;"><font style="border-left: none; border-right: none;">31</font>, <font style="border-left: none; border-right: none;">2016</font>&nbsp;and $<font class=" FactMarked">1,032</font>&nbsp;during the year ended December</font><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">&nbsp;</font><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;"><font style="border-left: none; border-right: none;">31</font>, <font style="border-left: none; border-right: none;">2015</font>.</font><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">&nbsp;</font><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">These losses are largely a result of our declining net interest income and increasing professional fees for problem asset resolution and additional costs associated with operating as a public company. &nbsp;</font><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">Despite these losses, the Bank&#8217;s total capital to risk-based capital ratio and Tier <font style="border-left: none; border-right: none;">1</font> leverage capital to average assets ratio was <font><font class=" FactMarked">14.5</font>% and <font class=" FactMarked">9.3</font>%</font> at December</font><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">&nbsp;</font><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">31, 2016. </font></p>
<p style="margin: 12pt 0pt 0pt;"><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">The Company has $<font class="TaggedFact Linked">314</font>&nbsp;and $<font class="TaggedFact">334</font>&nbsp;of cash at December</font><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">&nbsp;</font><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">31, 2016&nbsp;and December</font><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">&nbsp;</font><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">31, 2015.</font><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">&nbsp;</font><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">The Company completed the public offering of common stock in January 2015, raising $<font class="TaggedFact">2,504</font>, net of $<font class="TaggedFact">1,401</font> in conversion costs. The proceeds of the public stock offering were used to contribute $<font class=" FactMarked">2,000</font> of additional capital to the Bank. In addition, $<font class="TaggedFact">273</font> of the net proceeds were used to fund the loan to the employee stock ownership plan and approximately $<font class="TaggedFact">314</font>&nbsp;of the net proceeds were retained by Ben Franklin Financial, Inc.&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin: 12pt 0pt 0pt;"><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">On November</font><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">&nbsp;</font><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">25, <font style="border-left: none; border-right: none;">2015</font> the Bank entered into a revised Consent Order (the &#8220;New Order&#8221;) with the Office of the Comptroller of the Currency (&#8220;OCC&#8221;) that reduces the Bank&#8217;s regulatory compliance burden. Concurrent with the execution of the New Order, the Bank&#8217;s prior Consent Order (the &#8220;Old Order&#8221;) entered into between the Bank and the OCC dated December</font><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">&nbsp;</font><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;"><font style="border-left: none; border-right: none;">19</font>, <font style="border-left: none; border-right: none;">2012</font> was terminated. The New Order is comprised of <font class=" FactMarked">two</font> substantive articles as opposed to <font class=" FactMarked">12</font> substantive articles under the Old Order. The New Order reduced the Bank&#8217;s minimum required Tier <font style="border-left: none; border-right: none;">1</font> leverage capital ratio to <font class="TaggedFact">8</font>% from <font class="TaggedFact">9</font>% under the Old Consent Order and its minimum total risk-based capital ratio to <font class="TaggedFact">12</font>% from <font class="TaggedFact">13</font>% under the Old Consent Order. The New Consent Order requires the Bank to revise its current capital plan to include a capital distribution policy. Additionally, the New Order requires the Bank to revise its strategic plan to identify parameters and triggers which would cause the board of directors to market the Bank for merger or sale, in the event it failed to meet the <font class=" FactMarked">8</font>% and <font class=" FactMarked">12</font>% capital requirements under the New Order. The New Order continues to require quarterly reporting to the OCC and board monitoring requirements. At December</font><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">&nbsp;</font><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">31, 2016 and 2015 the Bank was in compliance with the required minimum ratios.&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin: 12pt 0pt 0pt;"><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">If the Bank is unable to meet the capital requirements and other requirements of the New Order, the OCC may institute other corrective measures and has enforcement powers to impose additional restrictions on the Bank&#8217;s operations, including seizure. Although management believes that it will successfully maintain the required capital ratios, there can be no assurance that they will be able to do so, nor that they will be able to comply fully with the provisions of the Order. Only the OCC has the ability to determine whether or not the provisions of the Order have been met.</font></p>

<p style="margin: 12pt 0pt 0pt;"><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;"><font style="font-size: 8pt;">&nbsp;</font>Anticipated maturities on mortgage-backed securities are not readily determinable as borrowers have the right to prepay their obligation with or without penalties.</font></p>

<p style="margin: 12pt 0pt 0pt;"><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">Unrealized losses on securities have not been recognized into income because the issuer&#8217;s securities are of high credit quality (rated AA or higher), management does not intend to sell and it is not more likely than not that management would be required to sell the securities prior to their anticipated recovery, and the decline in fair value is largely <font class=" FactMarked">due</font> to changes in interest rates. The fair value is expected to recover as the securities approach maturity.</font></p>

<p style="margin: 0pt;"><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 8pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin: 0pt;"><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt; font-weight: bold;">Credit Quality Indicators </font></p>
<p style="margin: 6pt 0pt 0pt;"><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">The Bank categorizes loans into risk categories based on relevant information about the ability of borrower to service their debt such as; current financial information, historical payment experience, credit documentation, public information, and current economic trends, among other factors. The Bank analyzes loans individually by classifying the loans as to credit risk. The analysis includes the non-homogeneous loans, such as multi- family, commercial real estate, construction, and commercial loans. The analysis performed on a quarterly basis. Homogeneous loans are monitored based on the past <font class=" FactMarked">due</font> status of the loan. The risk category of these loans is evaluated at origination, when a loan becomes delinquent or when a borrower requests a concession. </font></p>
<p style="margin: 18pt 0pt 0pt 24.45pt;"><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt; font-weight: bold;">Substandard </font></p>
<p style="margin: 6pt 0pt 0pt 24.45pt;"><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">Loans classified as substandard are inadequately protected by the current net worth and paying capacity of the obligor or of the collateral pledged, if any. Loans so classified have a well-defined weakness or weaknesses that jeopardize the liquidation of the debt. They are characterized by the distinct possibility that the institution will sustain some loss if the deficiencies are not corrected. </font></p>
<p style="margin: 18pt 0pt 0pt 24.45pt;"><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt; font-weight: bold;">Doubtful </font></p>
<p style="margin: 6pt 0pt 0pt 24.45pt;"><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">Loans classified as doubtful have all the weaknesses inherent in those classified as substandard, with the added characteristic that the weaknesses make collection or liquidation in full, on the basis of currently existing facts, conditions, and values, highly questionable and improbable. </font></p>
<p style="margin: 12pt 0pt 0pt;"><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">Loans not meeting the criteria above that are analyzed individually as part of the above described process are considered to be pass rated loans. </font><font class="TaggedFact"><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">As of December</font><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">&nbsp;</font><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;"><font class=" FactMarked">31</font>, <font class=" FactMarked">2016</font>, and December</font><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">&nbsp;</font><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;"><font class=" FactMarked">31</font>, <font class=" FactMarked">2015</font>&nbsp;and based on the most recent analysis performed, the risk category by loans is as follows:</font></font></p>

<p style="margin: 0pt; text-align: center;"><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">As of and for the Years Ended December 31, 2016 and <font class=" FactMarked">2015</font></font></p>
<p style="margin: 0pt; text-align: center;"><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">(Dollars in thousands except per share data) </font></p>
<p style="border-bottom-color: #000000; border-bottom-style: solid; border-bottom-width: 0.75pt; line-height: 12pt; margin: 0pt 0pt 2pt;"><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 12pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin: 0pt;"><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt; font-weight: bold;">NOTE <font class=" FactMarked">4</font> - LOANS RECEIVABLE </font><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">(Continued)</font></p>

<p style="margin: 0pt;"><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 8pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin: 0pt;"><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt; font-weight: bold;">Troubled Debt Restructurings </font></p>
<p style="margin: 6pt 0pt 0pt;"><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">Our troubled debt restructurings totaled $<font class="TaggedFact">1,576</font> and $<font class="TaggedFact">1,964</font>&nbsp;at December</font><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">&nbsp;</font><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;"><font class=" FactMarked">31</font>, <font class=" FactMarked">2016</font>&nbsp;and <font class=" FactMarked">2015</font>. There were <font class="OffLinkFact ParaMarked">no</font> loans modified as troubled debt restructurings during the years ended December</font><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">&nbsp;</font><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;"><font class=" FactMarked">31</font>, <font class=" FactMarked">2016</font>&nbsp;and <font class=" FactMarked">2015</font>. </font></p>
<p style="margin: 12pt 0pt 0pt;"><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">There were <font class="TaggedFact">two</font> loans modified as troubled debt restructurings with a balance of $<font class="TaggedFact">345</font> which are being reported as nonaccrual as of December</font><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">&nbsp;</font><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;"><font class=" FactMarked">31</font>, <font class=" FactMarked">2016</font>. &nbsp;There were <font class="TaggedFact">two</font> loans modified as troubled debt restructurings with a balance of $<font class="TaggedFact">415</font>&nbsp;which are being reported as nonaccrual as of December</font><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">&nbsp;</font><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;"><font class=" FactMarked">31</font>, <font class=" FactMarked">2015</font>, <font class="TaggedFact">one</font> of which totaling $<font class="TaggedFact">69</font>&nbsp;was paying as agreed under the terms of the modification. </font></p>
<p style="margin: 12pt 0pt 0pt;"><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">A loan is considered to be in payment default once it is <font class="TaggedFact">90</font> days contractually past <font class=" FactMarked">due</font> under the modified terms. During the year ended December</font><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">&nbsp;</font><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;"><font class=" FactMarked">31</font>, <font class=" FactMarked">2016</font>, <font class="TaggedFact">one</font> loan totaling<font> $<font><font class="NegatedFact">284</font></font></font>&nbsp;secured by a multi-family building had payments in default and is being reported as non-accrual. During&nbsp;the year ended December</font><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">&nbsp;</font><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;"><font class=" FactMarked">31</font>, <font class=" FactMarked">2015</font>&nbsp;there were <font class=" ParaMarked">no</font> payment defaults within 12 months following modification.</font></p>
<p style="margin: 12pt 0pt 0pt;"><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">At December</font><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">&nbsp;</font><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;"><font class=" FactMarked">31</font>, <font class=" FactMarked">2016</font>, the Company has allocated $<font class="TaggedFact">32</font> to specific reserves on $<font class="TaggedFact">1,231</font> of loans to customers whose loan terms have been modified in troubled debt restructurings. As of December</font><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">&nbsp;</font><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;"><font class=" FactMarked">31</font>, <font class=" FactMarked">2015</font>, the Company has allocated $<font class="TaggedFact">119</font> to specific reserves on $<font class="TaggedFact">1,271</font>&nbsp;of loans to customers whose loan terms have been modified in troubled debt restructurings. The Company has not committed to lend additional amounts as of December</font><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">&nbsp;</font><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;"><font class=" FactMarked">31</font>, <font class=" FactMarked">2016</font>&nbsp;and December</font><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">&nbsp;</font><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;"><font class=" FactMarked">31</font>, <font class=" FactMarked">2015</font>&nbsp;to customers with outstanding loans that are classified as troubled debt restructurings.</font></p>

<p style="margin: 0pt;"><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt; font-weight: bold;">NOTE <font class=" FactMarked">5</font> - PREMISES AND EQUIPMENT</font><br></p>

<p style="margin: 0pt; text-align: center;"><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">NOTES TO CONSOLIDATED FINANCIAL STATEMENTS </font></p>
<p style="margin: 0pt; text-align: center;"><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">As of and for the Years Ended December 31, 2016 and <font style="border-left: none; border-right: none;">2015</font></font></p>
<p style="margin: 0pt; text-align: center;"><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">(Dollars in thousands except per share data)</font></p>
<p style="border-bottom-color: #000000; border-bottom-style: solid; border-bottom-width: 0.75pt; line-height: 12pt; margin: 0pt 0pt 2pt;"><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 12pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin: 0pt;"><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 8pt;">&nbsp;</font></p><div class="TaggedFact">
<p style="margin: 0pt;"><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt; font-weight: bold;">NOTE 8</font><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">&nbsp;- </font><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt; font-weight: bold;">REGULATORY CAPITAL MATTERS</font><br></p>
<p style="margin: 6pt 0pt 0pt;"><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">The Bank is subject to various regulatory capital requirements administered by federal banking agencies. Capital adequacy guidelines and prompt corrective action regulations, involve quantitative measures of assets, liabilities, and certain off-balance-sheet items calculated under regulatory accounting practices. Capital amounts and classifications are also subject to qualitative judgments by regulators. Failure to meet capital requirements can initiate regulatory action. The final rules implementing Basel Committee on Banking Supervision&#8217;s capital guidelines for U.S. banks (Basel Ill rules) became effective for the Company on January</font><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">&nbsp;</font><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;"><font style="border-left: none; border-right: none;">1</font>, <font style="border-left: none; border-right: none;">2015</font> with full compliance with all of the requirements being phased in over a multi-year schedule, and fully phased in by January</font><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">&nbsp;</font><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;"><font style="border-left: none; border-right: none;">1</font>, <font style="border-left: none; border-right: none;">2019</font>. The net unrealized gain or loss on available for sale securities is not included in computing regulatory capital.&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin: 12pt 0pt 0pt;"><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">Quantitative measures established by regulation to help ensure capital adequacy require the Bank to maintain minimum amounts and ratios of total and Tier I capital as defined in the regulations to risk-weighted assets as defined and of Tier I capital to adjusted total assets as defined. To be categorized as well capitalized, the Bank must maintain minimum total risk-based, Tier I risk-based, and Tier I leverage ratios. On November</font><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">&nbsp;</font><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;"><font style="border-left: none; border-right: none;">25</font>, <font style="border-left: none; border-right: none;">2015</font> the Bank entered into a New Order with the OCC that reduces the Bank&#8217;s regulatory compliance burden. Concurrent with the execution of the New Order, the Old Order entered into between the Bank and the OCC dated December</font><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">&nbsp;</font><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;"><font style="border-left: none; border-right: none;">19</font>, <font style="border-left: none; border-right: none;">2012</font> was terminated. The New Order reduced the Bank&#8217;s minimum required Tier <font style="border-left: none; border-right: none;">1</font> leverage capital ratio to <font class="TaggedFact">8</font>% from <font class="TaggedFact">9</font>% under the Old Consent Order and its minimum total risk-based capital ratio to <font class="TaggedFact">12</font>% from <font class="TaggedFact">13</font>% under the Old Order. As a result of entering into the New Order to achieve and maintain specific capital levels, the Bank&#8217;s capital classification under the Prompt Corrective Action rules was &#8220;adequately capitalized&#8221; at December</font><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">&nbsp;</font><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;"><font style="border-left: none; border-right: none;">31</font>, <font style="border-left: none; border-right: none;">2016</font> and <font style="border-left: none; border-right: none;">2015</font>. While under the New and Old Order, the Bank cannot be consider &#8220;well capitalized&#8221;. </font></p>
<p style="margin: 12pt 0pt 0pt;"><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">The Company completed the public offering of common stock in January 2015, raising $<font class=" FactMarked">2,504</font><font>, net of $</font><font class=" FactMarked">1,401</font><font> i</font>n conversion costs. The proceeds of the public stock offering were used to contribute $<font class="TaggedFact">2,000</font> of additional capital to the Bank.&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin: 0pt;"><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 8pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin: 0pt;"><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">The prompt corrective action regulations provide <font class=" FactMarked">five</font> classifications, including well capitalized, adequately capitalized, undercapitalized, significantly undercapitalized, and critically undercapitalized, although these terms are not used to represent overall financial condition. If undercapitalized, asset growth and expansion are limited and plans for capital restoration are required. </font></p>
<p style="margin: 12pt 0pt 0pt;"><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">The allowance for loan losses is limited to <font class="TaggedFact">1.25</font>% of risk weighted assets. As of December</font><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">&nbsp;</font><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;"><font style="border-left: none; border-right: none;">31</font>, <font style="border-left: none; border-right: none;">2016</font>, and December</font><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">&nbsp;</font><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;"><font style="border-left: none; border-right: none;">31</font>, <font style="border-left: none; border-right: none;">2015</font>, $<font class="TaggedFact">225</font>&nbsp;and $<font class="TaggedFact">373</font>&nbsp;was excluded from the allowance for loan losses in the calculation of total regulatory capital. </font></p>
<p style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt;">&nbsp;</p>

<p style="border-bottom-color: #000000; border-bottom-style: solid; border-bottom-width: 0.75pt; line-height: 12pt; margin: 0pt 0pt 2pt;"><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 12pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin: 0pt;"><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt; font-weight: bold;">NOTE 9 - EMPLOYEE BENEFITS</font><br></p>
<p style="margin: 6pt 0pt 0pt;"><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">All share or per share amounts referenced in this note have be adjusted to reflect the conversion offering exchange ratio of <font class="FactMarked mceNonEditable">.3562</font>. </font></p>
<p style="margin: 12pt 0pt 0pt;"><font style="font-family: 'times new roman', times; font-size: 10pt;"><font>On October&nbsp;</font><font class="FactMarked mceNonEditable">18</font><font>, </font><font class="FactMarked mceNonEditable">2006</font><font>, the Company adopted an employee stock ownership plan (&#8220;the ESOP&#8221;) for the benefit of substantially all employees. The ESOP borrowed $</font><font class="TaggedFact mceNonEditable">778</font><font> from the Company and used those funds to acquire </font><font class="TaggedFact mceNonEditable">27,699</font><font> shares of the Company&#8217;s stock in connection with the reorganization at a price of $</font><font class="TaggedFact mceNonEditable">28.07</font><font> per share. On January&nbsp;22, 2015, the ESOP borrowed $</font><font class="TaggedFact mceNonEditable">273</font><font> from the Company and used those funds to acquire </font><font class="TaggedFact mceNonEditable">27,333</font><font> shares of the Company&#8217;s stock in connection with the reorganization at a price of $</font><font class="TaggedFact mceNonEditable">10.00</font><font> per share</font>.</font></p>
<p style="margin: 12pt 0pt 0pt;"><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;"><font style="font-family: 'times new roman', times;">Share</font>s purchased by the ESOP with the loan proceeds are held in a suspense account and are allocated to ESOP participants on a pro rata basis as principal and interest payments are made by the ESOP to the Company. The loan is secured by shares purchased with the loan proceeds and will be repaid by the ESOP with funds from the Company&#8217;s discretionary contributions to the ESOP and earnings on ESOP assets. During the years ended&nbsp;</font><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">December</font><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">&nbsp;</font><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;"><font class="FactMarked mceNonEditable">31</font>, <font class="FactMarked mceNonEditable">2016</font> and <font class="FactMarked mceNonEditable">2015</font>, the Company made contributions to the ESOP of $<font class="TaggedFact mceNonEditable">88</font>&nbsp;and $<font class="TaggedFact mceNonEditable">88</font>&nbsp;and the ESOP made the annual principal and interest payments on the loan of $<font class="TaggedFact mceNonEditable">88</font>&nbsp;and $<font class="TaggedFact mceNonEditable">88</font>.</font></p>
<p style="margin: 12pt 0pt 0pt;"><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">As shares are released from collateral, the Company reports compensation expense equal to the current market price of the shares and the shares become outstanding for earnings-per-share computations. Dividends on allocated ESOP shares reduce retained earnings; dividends on unearned ESOP shares reduce accrued interest. Because participants may require the Company to purchase their ESOP shares upon termination of their employment, the fair value of all earned and allocated ESOP shares may become a liability. During the years ended December</font><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">&nbsp;</font><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;"><font class="FactMarked mceNonEditable">31</font>, <font class="FactMarked mceNonEditable">2016</font> and <font class="FactMarked mceNonEditable">2015</font>, <font class="OffLinkFact ParaMarked mceNonEditable">no</font> ESOP shares were distributed to participants. </font></p>
<p style="margin: 12pt 0pt 0pt;"><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">The ESOP has a plan year end of December</font><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">&nbsp;</font><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;"><font class="FactMarked mceNonEditable">31</font>. Expense related to the ESOP was $<font class="TaggedFact mceNonEditable">36</font>&nbsp;and $<font class="TaggedFact mceNonEditable">35</font> for the years ended December</font><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">&nbsp;</font><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;"><font class="FactMarked mceNonEditable">31</font>, <font class="FactMarked mceNonEditable">2016</font> and <font class="FactMarked mceNonEditable">2015</font>. </font></p>
<p style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt;">&nbsp;</p>

<p style="margin: 12pt 0pt 0pt;"><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">On March</font><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">&nbsp;</font><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;"><font class="FactMarked mceNonEditable">26</font>, <font class="FactMarked mceNonEditable">2008</font>, stockholders of the Company approved the Ben Franklin Financial, Inc. Equity Incentive Plan (the &#8220;Plan&#8221;) which provides officers, employees, and directors of the Company and the Bank with stock based incentives to promote our growth and performance. The Plan shall remain in effect as long as any awards are outstanding provided, however, that no awards be granted under the plan after <font class="OffLinkFact FactMarked mceNonEditable">ten</font> years from the date of adoption. The Plan authorizes the issuance of up to <font class="TaggedFact mceNonEditable">48,473</font> shares of Company common stock pursuant to grants of incentive&nbsp;</font><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">and non-statutory stock options, stock appreciation rights, and restricted stock awards. No more than <font class="TaggedFact mceNonEditable">13,849</font> shares may be issued as restricted stock awards. No more than <font class="TaggedFact mceNonEditable">34,624</font> shares may be issued pursuant to stock options and stock appreciation rights, all of which may be granted pursuant to the exercise of incentive stock options. On April</font><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">&nbsp;</font><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;"><font class="FactMarked mceNonEditable">17</font>, <font class="FactMarked mceNonEditable">2008</font>, the Company granted restricted stock awards for <font class="TaggedFact mceNonEditable">12,275</font> common shares and stock options for <font class="TaggedFact mceNonEditable">30,896</font> common shares under the Plan, all of which vest over a <font class="OffLinkFact FactMarked mceNonEditable">five</font>-year period. Awards under the Plan may also fully vest upon the participant&#8217;s death or disability or change in control of the Company. All of the options granted have an exercise price of $<font class="TaggedFact mceNonEditable">26.28</font> per share, which was the closing price of the stock on the grant date, adjusted to reflect the conversion offering exchange ratio o<font>f </font><font class="FactMarked mceNonEditable">.3562</font><font>.</font> <font class="OffLinkFact ParaMarked mceNonEditable">No</font> options have been exercised or forfeited as of December</font><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">&nbsp;</font><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;"><font class="FactMarked mceNonEditable">31</font>, <font class="FactMarked mceNonEditable">2016</font>, and December</font><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">&nbsp;</font><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;"><font class="FactMarked mceNonEditable">31</font>, <font class="FactMarked mceNonEditable">2015</font></font><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt; font-weight: bold;">. </font><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">The options have <font class="OffLinkFact ParaMarked mceNonEditable">no</font> intrinsic value as of December</font><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">&nbsp;</font><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;"><font class="FactMarked mceNonEditable">31</font>, <font class="FactMarked mceNonEditable">2016</font>, and December</font><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">&nbsp;</font><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;"><font class="FactMarked mceNonEditable">31</font>, <font class="FactMarked mceNonEditable">2015</font>.</font></p>

<p style="margin: 0pt; text-align: center;"><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">NOTES TO CONSOLIDATED FINANCIAL STATEMENTS </font></p>
<p style="margin: 0pt; text-align: center;"><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">As of and for the Years Ended December 31, 2016 and <font class="FactMarked mceNonEditable">2015</font></font></p>
<p style="margin: 0pt; text-align: center;"><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">(Dollars in thousands except per share data) </font></p>
<p style="border-bottom-color: #000000; border-bottom-style: solid; border-bottom-width: 0.75pt; line-height: 12pt; margin: 0pt 0pt 2pt;"><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 12pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin: 0pt;"><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 8pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin: 0pt;"><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt; font-weight: bold;">NOTE <font style="/* background-color: #d1d2f9;"><font class="FactMarked mceNonEditable">9</font></font>&nbsp;- EMPLOYEE BENEFITS </font><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">(Continued)</font></p>
</div>
<p style="margin: 12pt 0pt 0pt;"><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">The fair value of each option award is estimated on the date of grant using a closed form option valuation (Black-Scholes). Since the Company stock had been outstanding less than <font class="OffLinkFact FactMarked mceNonEditable">two</font> years at the time of the grant, expected volatilities as of the </font><font class="TaggedFact mceNonEditable"><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">April</font><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">&nbsp;</font><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;"><font class="FactMarked mceNonEditable">17</font>, <font class="FactMarked mceNonEditable">2008</font></font></font><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;"> grant date were based on historical stock price volatilities of other micro-cap banks and bank holding companies. The expected term represents the period of time that options granted are expected to be outstanding, which takes into account that the options are not transferable. The risk-free interest rate for the expected term of the option is based on the U.S. Treasury yield curve in effect at the time of the grant. <font class="OffLinkFact ParaMarked mceNonEditable">No</font> stock options were granted in <font class="FactMarked mceNonEditable">2016</font> and <font class="FactMarked mceNonEditable">2015</font>. There was <font class="OffLinkFact ParaMarked mceNonEditable">no</font> stock option expense for the year ended December</font><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">&nbsp;</font><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;"><font class="FactMarked mceNonEditable">31</font>, <font class="FactMarked mceNonEditable">2016</font> and <font class="FactMarked mceNonEditable">2015</font> since the stock options were fully vested prior to January</font><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">&nbsp;</font><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;"><font class="FactMarked mceNonEditable">1</font>, <font class="FactMarked mceNonEditable">2015</font>. </font></p>
<p style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt;">&nbsp;</p>

<p style="margin: 12pt 0pt 0pt;"><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">The fair value of the restricted stock awards was $<font class="TaggedFact mceNonEditable">26.28</font> per share, which was the closing price of the stock on the April</font><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">&nbsp;</font><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;"><font class="FactMarked mceNonEditable">17</font>, <font class="FactMarked mceNonEditable">2008</font> grant date, adjusted to reflect the conversion offering exchange ratio of <font class="TaggedFact mceNonEditable">.<font style="border-left: none; border-right: none;">3562</font></font>. At December</font><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">&nbsp;</font><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;"><font class="FactMarked mceNonEditable">31</font>, <font class="FactMarked mceNonEditable">2016</font> and <font class="FactMarked mceNonEditable">2015</font>, there were <font class="TaggedFact mceNonEditable">12,275</font> restricted stock awards vested and <font class="OffLinkFact ParaMarked mceNonEditable">none</font> forfeited. There was <font class="OffLinkFact ParaMarked mceNonEditable">no</font> restricted stock award expense for the years ended December</font><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">&nbsp;</font><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;"><font class="FactMarked mceNonEditable">31</font>, <font class="FactMarked mceNonEditable">2016</font> and <font class="FactMarked mceNonEditable">2015</font> since the restricted stock was fully vested prior to January</font><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">&nbsp;</font><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;"><font class="FactMarked mceNonEditable">1</font>, <font class="FactMarked mceNonEditable">2015</font>. As of December</font><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">&nbsp;</font><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;"><font class="FactMarked mceNonEditable">31</font>, <font class="FactMarked mceNonEditable">2016</font> and <font class="FactMarked mceNonEditable">2015</font>, there was <font class="OffLinkFact ParaMarked mceNonEditable">no</font> unrecognized compensation cost related to non-vested shares granted under the Plan.</font><br></p>
<p style="margin: 12pt 0pt 0pt;"><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">The value of stock options and restricted stock awards as of the grant date were expensed over the <font class="FactMarked mceNonEditable">five</font>-year vesting period.</font></p>
<p style="margin: 12pt 0pt 0pt;"><font><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;"><font>On May 25</font><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;" class="selected"><font>, <font style="border-left: none; border-right: none;" class="selected">2016</font>,</font> stockholders of the Company approved the Ben Franklin Financial, Inc.<font style="border-left: none; border-right: none;">2016</font> Equity Incentive Plan (the &#8220;<font style="border-left: none; border-right: none;">2016</font> Plan&#8221;) which provides officers, employees, and directors of the Company and the Bank with stock based incentives to promote our growth and performance. The Plan shall remain in effect as long as any awards are outstanding provided, however, that <font class="OffLinkFact ParaMarked mceNonEditable">no</font> awards be granted under the plan after <font class="OffLinkFact FactMarked mceNonEditable">ten</font> years from the date of adoption. The Plan authorizes the issuance of up to&nbsp;<font class="TaggedFact mceNonEditable">54,666</font> shares of Company common stock pursuant to grants of incentive&nbsp;and non-statutory stock options, stock appreciation rights, and restricted stock awards. No more than <font class="TaggedFact mceNonEditable">15,619</font> shares may be issued as restricted stock awards. No more than <font class="TaggedFact mceNonEditable">39,047</font> shares may be issued pursuant to stock options and stock appreciation rights, all of which may be granted pursuant to the exercise of incentive stock options. On January 24<font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;" class="selected">, <font style="border-left: none; border-right: none;">2017</font>, the Company granted restricted stock awards for <font class="TaggedFact mceNonEditable">15,619</font> common shares and stock options for <font class="TaggedFact mceNonEditable">39,047</font> common shares under the Plan, all of which vest over a <font class="OffLinkFact FactMarked mceNonEditable">three</font> year period. Awards under the Plan may also fully vest upon the participant&#8217;s death or disability or change in control of the Company. All of the options granted have an exercise price of $<font class="TaggedFact mceNonEditable">10.70</font> per share, which was the closing price of the stock on the grant date.</font></font></font></font></p>

<p style="margin: 0pt; text-align: center;"><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">As of and for the Years Ended December 31, 2016 and 2015</font></p>
<p style="margin: 0pt; text-align: center;"><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">(Dollars in thousands except per share data) </font></p>
<p style="border-bottom-color: #000000; border-bottom-style: solid; border-bottom-width: 0.75pt; line-height: 12pt; margin: 0pt 0pt 2pt;"><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 12pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin: 0pt;"><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 8pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin: 0pt;"><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt; font-weight: bold;">NOTE 10 - INCOME TAXES </font><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">(Continued)</font></p>
</div>
<p style="margin: 0pt;"><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 8pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin: 0pt;"><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">The Company established a valuation allowance for net deferred tax assets based on management&#8217;s assessment of the ability to realize the deferred tax asset primarily based on the tax losses incurred in recent years and, under current law, the inability to recover any additional taxes paid in prior years. As of December</font><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">&nbsp;</font><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">31, 2016, state net operating losses of <font>$<font class="TaggedFact mceNonEditable">9,167</font></font>&nbsp;are being carried forward and will be available to reduce future taxable income. These state net operating loss carryforwards will expire beginning in <font class="TaggedFact mceNonEditable">2019</font> through <font class="TaggedFact mceNonEditable">2028</font>&nbsp;if not utilized to reduce future taxable income. </font></p>
<p style="margin: 12pt 0pt 0pt;"><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">The Company&#8217;s net operating losses for federal income taxes were $<font><font class="TaggedFact mceNonEditable">7,396</font></font> and $<font class="TaggedFact mceNonEditable">6,063</font>&nbsp;as of December</font><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">&nbsp;</font><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">31, 2016 and 2015 of which $<font class="FactMarked mceNonEditable">7,396</font>&nbsp;are being carried forward to reduce taxable income in future years. These federal net operating loss carryforwards will begin to expire in <font class="TaggedFact mceNonEditable">2030</font>. </font></p>
<p style="margin: 12pt 0pt 0pt;"><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">The Company is subject to federal income tax as well as income tax of the state of Illinois. The Company is no longer subject to examination by taxing authorities for years before 2013.</font></p>

<p style="margin: 0pt;"><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt; font-weight: bold;">NOTE 12 - COMMITMENTS AND FINANCIAL INSTRUMENTS WITH OFF-BALANCE-SHEET RISK</font><br></p>
<p style="margin: 6pt 0pt 0pt;"><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">The Bank is a party to financial instruments with off-balance-sheet risk in the normal course of business to meet the financing needs of its customers. These financial instruments consist of commitments to make loans and fund unused lines of credit and loans in process. The Bank follows the same credit policy to make such commitments as is followed for those loans recorded on the statement of financial condition. <font class="TaggedFact">The contractual amounts of financial instruments with off-balance-sheet risk at year end were as follows:</font></font></p>

<p style="margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt;"><br></p><div class="TaggedFact">
<p style="margin: 0pt;"><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt; font-weight: bold;">NOTE 13 - FAIR VALUE MEASURES</font><br></p>
<p style="margin: 8pt 0pt 0pt;"><font style="font-family: 'times new roman', times; font-size: 10pt;">Fair value is the exchange price that would be received for an asset or paid to transfer a liability (exit price) in the principal or most advantageous market for the asset or liability in an orderly transaction between market participants on the measurement date. There are <font class=" FactMarked">three</font> levels of inputs that may be used to measure fair values: </font></p>
<p style="margin: 6pt 0pt 0pt 48.95pt;"><font style="font-family: 'times new roman', times; font-size: 10pt;">Level <font style="border-left: none; border-right: none;">1</font> &#8211; Quoted prices (unadjusted) for identical assets or liabilities in active markets that the entity has the ability to access as of the measurement date. </font></p>
<p style="margin: 6pt 0pt 0pt 48.95pt;"><font style="font-family: 'times new roman', times; font-size: 10pt;">Level <font style="border-left: none; border-right: none;">2</font> &#8211; Significant other observable inputs other than Level <font style="border-left: none; border-right: none;">1</font> prices such as quoted prices for similar assets or liabilities; quoted prices in markets that are not active; or other inputs that are observable or can be corroborated by observable market data. </font></p>
<p style="margin: 6pt 0pt 0pt 48.95pt;"><font style="font-family: 'times new roman', times; font-size: 10pt;">Level <font style="border-left: none; border-right: none;">3</font> &#8211; Significant unobservable inputs that reflect a company&#8217;s own assumptions about the assumptions that market participants would use in pricing an asset or liability. </font></p>
<p style="margin: 12pt 0pt 0pt;"><font style="font-family: 'times new roman', times; font-size: 10pt;">The Company used the following methods and significant assumptions to estimate the fair value of each type of financial instrument: </font></p>
<p style="margin: 12pt 0pt 0pt;"><font style="font-family: 'times new roman', times; font-size: 10pt;"><font style="text-decoration: underline;">Securities Available-for-Sale</font>: The fair values of securities available-for-sale are determined by matrix pricing, which is a mathematical technique widely used in the industry to value debt securities without relying exclusively on quoted prices for the specific securities but rather by relying on the securities&#8217; relationship to other benchmark quoted securities (Level <font class=" FactMarked">2</font> inputs). </font></p>
<div class="ExcludeValue">
<p style="border-bottom-color: #000000; border-bottom-style: solid; border-bottom-width: 0.75pt; line-height: 12pt; margin: 0pt 0pt 2pt;"><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 12pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin: 0pt; text-align: center;"><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">BEN FRANKLIN FINANCIAL, INC. </font></p>
<p style="margin: 0pt; text-align: center;"><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">NOTES TO CONSOLIDATED FINANCIAL STATEMENTS </font></p>
<p style="margin: 0pt; text-align: center;"><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">As of and for the Years Ended December 31, 2016 and <font class=" FactMarked">2015</font></font></p>
<p style="margin: 0pt; text-align: center;"><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">(Dollars in thousands except per share data) </font></p>
<p style="border-bottom-color: #000000; border-bottom-style: solid; border-bottom-width: 0.75pt; line-height: 12pt; margin: 0pt 0pt 2pt;"><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 12pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin: 0pt;"><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 8pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin: 0pt;"><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt; font-weight: bold;">NOTE <font class=" FactMarked">13</font>&nbsp;- FAIR VALUE MEASURES</font><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;"> (Continued)</font><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt; font-weight: bold;"> </font></p>
</div>
<p style="margin: 0pt;"><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 8pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin: 0pt;"><font style="font-family: 'times new roman', times; font-size: 10pt;"><font style="text-decoration: underline;">Impaired Loans</font>:&nbsp;The fair value of impaired loans with specific allocations of the allowance for loan losses is generally based on recent real estate appraisals. These appraisals may utilize a single valuation approach or a combination of approaches including comparable sales and the income approach. Adjustments are routinely made in the appraisal process by the independent appraisers to adjust for differences between the comparable sales and income data available. Such adjustments are usually significant and typically result in a Level <font class=" FactMarked">3</font> classification of the inputs for determining fair value.&nbsp;Non-real estate collateral may be valued using an appraisal, net book value per the borrower&#8217;s financial statements, or aging reports, adjusted or discounted based on management&#8217;s historical knowledge, changes in market conditions from the time of the valuation, and management&#8217;s expertise and knowledge of the client and client&#8217;s business, resulting in a Level <font class=" FactMarked">3</font> fair value classification.&nbsp;Impaired loans are evaluated on a quarterly basis for additional impairment and adjusted accordingly.</font></p>
<p style="margin: 12pt 0pt 0pt;"><font style="font-family: 'times new roman', times; font-size: 10pt;"><font style="text-decoration: underline;">Repossessed Assets</font>: Assets acquired through or instead of loan foreclosure are initially recorded at fair value less costs to sell when acquired, establishing a new cost basis.&nbsp;These assets are subsequently accounted for at lower of cost or fair value less estimated costs to sell. Fair value is commonly based on recent real estate appraisals which are updated no less frequently than annually. These appraisals may utilize a single valuation approach or a combination of approaches including comparable sales and the income approach. Adjustments are routinely made in the appraisal process by the independent appraisers to adjust for differences between the comparable sales and income data available. Such adjustments are usually significant and typically result in a Level <font style="border-left: none; border-right: none;">3</font> classification of the inputs for determining fair value.&nbsp;Other real estate owned properties are evaluated on a quarterly basis for additional impairment and adjusted accordingly.</font></p>
<p style="margin: 12pt 0pt 0pt;"><font style="font-family: 'times new roman', times; font-size: 10pt;">Appraisals for both collateral-dependent impaired loans and other real estate owned are performed by certified appraisers whose qualifications and licenses have been reviewed and verified by the Company.&nbsp;Once received, management reviews the assumptions and approaches utilized in the appraisal as well as the overall resulting fair value in comparison with independent data sources such as recent market data or industry-wide statistics.&nbsp;</font><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">Upon sale of collateral, the Company compares the actual selling price of collateral that has been sold to the most recent appraised value to determine what additional adjustment should be made to the appraisal value to arrive at fair value for the remaining assets carried at fair value. </font></p>

<p style="margin: 6pt 0pt 0pt;"><font style="font-family: 'times new roman', times;"><font style="font-size: 10pt;">Impaired loans, which are measured for impairment using the fair value of the collateral (less cost to sell) for collateral dependent loans, had an aggregate balance o<font>f $<font style="border-left: none; border-right: none;"><font class="TaggedFact">1,714</font></font>&nbsp;with a $<font style="border-left: none; border-right: none;"><font class="TaggedFact">10</font></font></font>&nbsp;valuation allowance at December</font><font style="font-size: 10pt;">&nbsp;</font><font style="font-size: 10pt;"><font style="border-left: none; border-right: none;"><font style="border-left: none; border-right: none;">31</font></font>, <font style="border-left: none; border-right: none;"><font style="border-left: none; border-right: none;">2016</font></font>. The impaired loans resulted in $<font class="TaggedFact">0</font>&nbsp;provision for loan loss for the year ended December</font><font style="font-size: 10pt;">&nbsp;</font><font style="font-size: 10pt;"><font style="border-left: none; border-right: none;"><font style="border-left: none; border-right: none;">31</font></font>, <font style="border-left: none; border-right: none;"><font style="border-left: none; border-right: none;">2016</font></font>. At December</font><font style="font-size: 10pt;">&nbsp;</font><font style="font-size: 10pt;"><font style="border-left: none; border-right: none;"><font style="border-left: none; border-right: none;">31</font></font>, <font style="border-left: none; border-right: none;"><font style="border-left: none; border-right: none;">2015</font></font>, impaired loans had an aggregate balance of $<font class="TaggedFact">1,454</font> with a $<font class="TaggedFact">52</font>&nbsp;valuation allowance. The impaired loans resulted in $<font class="TaggedFact">259</font> provision for loan loss for the year ended December</font><font style="font-size: 10pt;">&nbsp;</font><font style="font-size: 10pt;"><font style="border-left: none; border-right: none;"><font style="border-left: none; border-right: none;">31</font></font>, <font style="border-left: none; border-right: none;"><font style="border-left: none; border-right: none;">2015</font></font>.</font></font><br></p>
<p style="margin: 12pt 0pt 0pt;"><font style="font-family: 'times new roman', times;"><font style="font-size: 10pt;">Repossessed assets, consisting of other real estate owned, repossessed automobiles, and other repossessed assets are measured at the lower of cost or fair value less costs to sell. Repossessed assets were carried at <font>$<font style="border-left: none; border-right: none;"><font class="TaggedFact">408</font></font>&nbsp;</font>at December</font><font style="font-size: 10pt;">&nbsp;</font><font style="font-size: 10pt;"><font style="border-left: none; border-right: none;"><font style="border-left: none; border-right: none;">31</font></font>, <font style="border-left: none; border-right: none;"><font style="border-left: none; border-right: none;">2016</font></font> consisting of the cost basis of $<font style="border-left: none; border-right: none;"><font class="TaggedFact">643</font></font>&nbsp;and a valuation allowance of $<font style="border-left: none; border-right: none;"><font class="TaggedFact">235</font></font>. Repossessed assets were carried at $<font class="TaggedFact">87</font> at December</font><font style="font-size: 10pt;">&nbsp;</font><font style="font-size: 10pt;"><font style="border-left: none; border-right: none;"><font style="border-left: none; border-right: none;">31</font></font>, <font style="border-left: none; border-right: none;"><font style="border-left: none; border-right: none;">2015</font></font>, consisting of the cost basis of $<font class="TaggedFact">101</font>&nbsp;and a valuation allowance of $<font class="TaggedFact">14</font>. Write-downs on repossessed assets were $<font style="border-left: none; border-right: none;"><font class="TaggedFact">68</font></font>&nbsp;for the year ended December</font><font style="font-size: 10pt;">&nbsp;</font><font style="font-size: 10pt;"><font style="border-left: none; border-right: none;"><font style="border-left: none; border-right: none;">31</font></font>, <font style="border-left: none; border-right: none;"><font style="border-left: none; border-right: none;">2016</font></font>. Write-downs on repossessed assets were $<font class="TaggedFact">14</font>&nbsp;for the year ended December</font><font style="font-size: 10pt;">&nbsp;</font><font style="font-size: 10pt;"><font style="border-left: none; border-right: none;"><font style="border-left: none; border-right: none;">31</font></font>, <font style="border-left: none; border-right: none;"><font style="border-left: none; border-right: none;">2015</font></font>.</font></font></p>

<p style="margin: 0pt;"><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;"><br>The methods and assumptions, not previously presented, used to estimate fair values are described as follows:</font><br></p>
<p style="margin: 18pt 0pt 0pt 24.45pt; margin-left: 4%;"><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt; font-style: italic;">(a) Cash and Cash Equivalents </font></p>
<p style="margin: 6pt 0pt 0pt 48.95pt; margin-left: 8%;"><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">The carrying amounts of cash and short-term instruments approximate fair values and are classified as Level <font class=" FactMarked">1</font>. </font></p>
